articles.title: Fantasy Football Waiver Wire: Plenty of impact talent available to boost college lineups going into Week 2
articles.summary: Eric Froton reveals his top waiver adds heading into Week 2 of the college fantasy football season.
articles.body:
It was a wild and eventful Week 1 of the college fantasy football season, with plenty of surprises from a CFF standpoint that we need to account for. For the most part, I'm going to be striving to keep the waiver-wire targets below a 50% roster rate, but I made an exception for two important widely-available players who should be in the 90% range. Let's dive in on the top players to add for Week 2.

QB Mason Heintschel, Pittsburgh - 9% Rostered

My top QB sleeper for 2026, Heintschel delivered Week's 1 most prolific fantasy quarterback performance of Week 1 , shredding Miami (OH) for 453 yards, seven touchdowns and 48.42 fantasy points while completing 31-of-41 passes in Pitt's 59-14 victory. The sophomore averaged 11.0 YPA, avoided any turnovers and added 23 rushing yards, with his seven touchdown passes tying the Pitt single-game record while establishing a new ACC mark.

Heintschel's distribution was particularly encouraging from a fantasy perspective, as seven different Panthers caught touchdown passes, suggesting OC Kade Bell has constructed an offense capable of generating production regardless of which receiver emerges as the alpha. Heintschel also demonstrated this ceiling as a freshman, throwing for 300+ yards four times after taking over the starting job from Eli Holstein.

While we should temper expectations of another seven-touchdown eruption, Pitt threw 41 times despite winning by 45 points. This is an extremely encouraging indicator that Bell intends to keep his foot on the accelerator, while Heintschel's 23 rushing yards provide a stable floor for CFF purposes. With UCF up next, Heintschel should immediately enter the weekly QB1/2 conversation and possess enough volume-driven upside to become one of 2026 CFF's biggest quarterback breakouts.

QB Anthony Colandrea, Nebraska - 6% Rostered

Colandrea wasn't exactly hiding from the CFF community after earning Mountain West Offensive Player of the Year honors at UNLV last season, but his Nebraska debut meaningfully increased his value. Colandrea threw for 275 yards and three touchdowns while running for another score in Nebraska's 49-21 victory over Ohio. He directed an offense that generated 523 total yards and erupted for 35 second-half points after a sluggish opening 30 minutes.

His production could be sustainable at least in the short term, as Colandrea rushed for 621 yards and nine touchdowns at UNLV last season after accumulating more than 500 rushing yards during his two years at Virginia, so his 31.3 Fantasy Points in Week 1 wasn't an aberration. Nebraska's dynamic backfield should make defenses respect the run, and Colandrea's established dual-threat profile gives him enticing upside. He's already moving from streaming territory toward every-week starter consideration against Nebraska's CFF-friendly early-season schedule, with the Huskers facing Bowling Green, North Dakota, @ Michigan State and Maryland over the next four weeks.

QB Faizon Brandon, Tennessee - 9% Rostered

Well, that escalated quickly. Brandon made his collegiate debut by completing 13-of-17 passes for 226 yards and three touchdowns while adding 68 rushing yards and two more scores on 10 carries in Tennessee's 56-9 destruction of Furman. The true freshman rolled up a gaudy 39.84 fantasy points despite the Volunteers having little reason to expose him once the game got out of hand.

The passing efficiency was encouraging, but the 10 rushing attempts are the statistic that should have CFF managers prioritizing him on the waiver wire and their FAB. Brandon wasn't merely scrambling when protection broke down; Tennessee clearly appears comfortable utilizing his athleticism as a fundamental component of the offense. A quarterback capable of providing 50-plus rushing yards with legitimate goal-line equity in HC Josh Heupel's potent system has immediate QB1 upside. Brandon's growing pains will eventually arrive, but his combination of rushing floor, supporting cast and offensive environment makes him a must add against Georgia Tech and Kennesaw State the next two weeks.

We can safely say the Nebraska backfield hierarchy looks considerably different today than it did Saturday morning. True freshman RB Jamal Rule was technically listed as a co-starter alongside Mekhi Nelson and Isaiah Mozee, but was the third Nebraska running back to enter the game. He proceeded to seize control of the position, converting a team-high 15 carries into 122 yards and two rushing touchdowns while catching two passes for another 47 yards and a score. Rule was particularly devastating after halftime, ripping off 106 yards on just eight carries while Nebraska overwhelmed Ohio en route to a 49-21 victory.

Rule's 17 touches produced 169 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns, which is the type of performance that can instantly reshuffle a depth chart. The January enrollee became Nebraska's first freshman running back since 2004 to eclipse 100 rushing yards in a season opener while averaging 8.1 YPC. Most importantly for CFF purposes, this wasn't garbage-time production from a fourth-stringer — Rule received goal-line work, caught a touchdown and led the Huskers in carries. There's still competition here, but Rule just transformed himself from a speculative freshman into one of the premier Power Four waiver targets heading into Week 2.

J'Koby Williams, Texas Tech - 21% Rostered

Williams entered 2026 as one of the most electric complementary backs in the Power Four after producing 868 rushing yards on just 155 carries (5.6 YPC) last season while sharing the Texas Tech backfield with Cameron Dickey last year. He made a compelling case for an immediate CFF waiver claim in Texas Tech's 33-10 victory over Abilene Christian, leading the Red Raiders with 71 rushing yards and a touchdown on 13 carries while adding a team-high eight receptions for 57 yards.

Williams finished with 128 scrimmage yards on 21 touches, averaging 5.5 YPC and scoring on a five-yard run in the first quarter. Most importantly for fantasy purposes, his eight receptions dwarfed the two catches recorded by fellow RB Dickey and demonstrated that Williams has a clearly defined passing-down role and chemistry with QB Will Hammond. The backfield remains crowded, as Dickey handled 14 carries for 48 yards while Quinten Joyner received 10 attempts for 43 yards and a touchdown, meaning Williams isn't walking into a traditional bell-cow workload. However, Williams was easily the most productive member of the trio, and 21 touches in a competitive portion of the game is enough volume to command CFF Waiver Wire priority at his meager 21% rostered rate.

Cam Edwards, Michigan State - 67% Rostered

Perhaps the most actionable RB usage development of Week 1 occurred in East Lansing, where UConn transfer RB Cam Edwards received a whopping 27 carries for 98 yards and a touchdown in Michigan State's 30-20 victory over Toledo. Edwards also caught two passes for seven yards, giving him 29 total opportunities in his Spartan debut. The 27 rushing attempts established a collegiate career high for Edwards and were especially notable considering no Michigan State running back handled more than 18 carries in a game last season.

The 3.6 YPC isn't going to generate breathless waiver-wire enthusiasm, but that's precisely why savvy CFF managers should be paying attention. Efficiency fluctuates, but 27 carries don't happen by accident. Michigan State handed Edwards the ball eight times on its opening possession alone, with the veteran finishing that drive by punching in a 2-yard touchdown from the Wildcat formation. He entered the season outside the upper echelon of CFF backs, but Week 1 suggests Michigan State intends to deploy him as a genuine workhorse as he received one of the largest workloads of any Power Four back in the country. He is an automatic start against MAC opponent Eastern Michigan in Week 2.

Purdue's season-opening 44-19 victory over Indiana State provided our first look at Minnesota transfer RB Fame Ijeboi in a Boilermakers uniform, and the sophomore made a compelling case for an expanded role. Ijeboi turned 11 carries into 87 yards and a touchdown while catching both of his targets for another 30 yards, producing 117 yards from scrimmage on just 13 touches. His 7.9 YPC rushing average was impressive enough, but Purdue also trusted him with a direct snap near the goal line that Ijeboi converted into a touchdown.

That's the combination we're striving to find on the waiver wire: efficiency, receiving involvement and access to high-value touches. Ijeboi entered Week 1 well outside the top 60 in most CFF RB discussions despite earning preseason Doak Walker recognition, but he looked like Purdue's most dangerous runner when given opportunities. The 11 carries aren't enough to declare him a bell-cow back, and Purdue is arguably the worst team in the Big Ten who plays one of the top-10 toughest schedules. However, 117 scrimmage yards on 13 touches with receiving and goal-line involvement is enough to make Ijeboi a preferred speculative addition who can start at your flex spot when the matchup is favorable.

Cataurus "Blue" Hicks, Pittsburgh - 9% Rostered

When a quarterback throws seven touchdown passes to seven different players, figuring out which receiver actually matters becomes a little complicated. Fortunately, Pitt gave us a fairly obvious clue. Hicks led the Panthers with nine targets and 114 receiving yards in their 59-14 rout of Miami (Ohio), while also catching one of Heintschel's record-tying seven touchdown passes. Pitt generated 453 passing yards and 646 total yards, creating one of Week 1's most impressive offensive performances.

The nine targets are far more indicative of his future utility than the touchdown. Heintschel spread his seven scoring passes among Hicks, Malik Knight, Censere Lee, Bryce Yates and several others, so chasing each touchdown recipient would be a classic early-season waiver mistake. Hicks, conversely, led the Panthers in routes (34) targets (9) and receiving yards (114), providing evidence that his production was supported by opportunity rather than touchdown variance. If Heintschel is taking the sophomore leap his opener suggests, Hicks could be one of the more consequential early-season CFF receiver discoveries.

Jeremiah McClellan, Oregon - 4% Rostered

McClellan authored one of Week 1's biggest CFF breakouts, catching six passes for 150 yards and a touchdown in Oregon's 34-27 victory over Boise State. The junior averaged a blistering 25.0 yards per reception, highlighted by a 51-yard catch-and-run, while his 8-yard third-quarter touchdown gave Oregon its first lead of the afternoon. It was easily the best performance of McClellan's career, nearly doubling his previous career high of 83 receiving yards. Most importantly for CFF managers, McClellan produced 24.0 fantasy points, an enormous return for a receiver who was largely an afterthought in drafts, as his 4% roster rate will attest.

There is legitimate competition for targets in Eugene, with Evan Stewart and Dakorien Moore also commanding substantial roles, so we shouldn't automatically project McClellan for WR1 volume every week. However, emerging as Heisman contending QB Dante Moore's trusted security blanket in a competitive opener carries considerably more weight than torching an overmatched FCS opponent. McClellan showed he can win downfield, create after the catch and secure tough contested throws in third-down situations, giving him multiple avenues to CFF production. In an Oregon offense capable of generating eye-popping passing numbers every week, McClellan is a priority Power Four waiver claim and should be rostered in virtually every CFF format following his 24-point eruption.

There are efficient performances, and then there's scoring three touchdowns on four offensive touches. Glasker caught three passes for 65 yards and two touchdowns while adding a 16-yard rushing touchdown on a jet sweep in BYU's 63-7 demolition of Utah Tech. All three scores came in the first half, with Glasker becoming the first BYU player since 2022 to score three touchdowns before halftime.

With the game effectively on ice at halftime, I'm not remotely concerned about Glasker's limited touches. The jet-sweep carry particularly matters because it demonstrates that the Cougars are actively manufacturing opportunities for the true freshman rather than simply waiting for targets to find him. He's exactly the type of impactful freshman I'd rather roster a week too early than attempt to acquire after he goes off against Arizona and Colorado State when he will receive a more expansive workload. With BYU's receiving room in flux heading into the season, Glasker is the clear waiver wire priority and projects as a high-volume WR1 for BYU who should be a weekly WR2/flex option.

The return of QB Steve Angeli was one of Syracuse's biggest offseason storylines, but Hatcher might have provided the most important CFF development from the Orange's 66-3 demolition of New Hampshire. Hatcher erupted for eight receptions, 147 yards and two touchdowns, accounting for more than half of Syracuse's 275 passing yards. Angeli looked healthy in his return from last season's Achilles injury, completing 20-of-29 passes for 263 yards and three touchdowns, with Hatcher emerging as his dominant receiving option.

That's precisely the type of Week 1 usage we're looking to attack. Syracuse entered the opener with uncertainty surrounding its receiving corps, with Tyshawn Russell absent and other pieces shuffled around the depth chart. Hatcher didn't merely capitalize with one long touchdown — eight receptions indicate projectable volume, while 147 yards and two scores demonstrate the ceiling attached to it. The competition obviously gets tougher from here, but a potential WR1 for Syracuse attached to a healthy Angeli warrants heavy waiver consideration.

Mini made an immediate case for increased CFF attention in Cal's opener against UCLA, hauling in four receptions for 58 yards and a touchdown. The 6-foot-4, 245-pound redshirt junior was already a proven contributor after posting 35 receptions for 387 yards and four touchdowns in 2025, but his Week 1 performance showed another step forward as a receiving weapon. Mini found the end zone against the Bruins and generated 17.0 yards per reception, an encouraging development at a position where explosive plays are difficult to find. His production translated to 13.8 fantasy points in Yahoo's default scoring, easily outperforming preseason expectations.

The waiver-wire appeal is particularly interesting because Mini entered the season with some uncertainty surrounding his role following the arrival of New Mexico transfer Dorian Thomas. Mini missed spring practice while recovering from an undisclosed injury, but returned for fall camp and clearly remains an important component of the Bears' passing attack. I had him ranked as my TE10 heading into Week 1, and that ranking has been wholly justified. With an established receiving résumé and a strong opening performance, Mini deserves to be the most aggressively pursued Power Four tight end on this week's waiver wire.

Listed as a co-starter on the initial OU depth chart, Beers made an immediate impression in the Sooners' 51-0 demolition of UTEP, taking a 15-yard out-breaker from QB John Mateer and hurdling a defender near the goal line before finishing the play for a 40-yard touchdown. For added measure, Beers appeared to score a second touchdown before the play was wiped out because fellow TE Jack VanDorselaer was called for an illegal pick, so his solid 11.3 fantasy points could have approached the 20-point mark with a little luck.

His nose for the goal line is vital considering TE is the most touchdown-dependent position in CFF. Oklahoma schemed opportunities for Beers, and Mateer threw three touchdowns while the Sooners piled up 51 points despite taking their foot off the gas. One game isn't enough to declare Beers an every-week TE1, but two would-be touchdown receptions in his first game demands our attention. He's one of my favorite speculative TE waiver additions because the acquisition cost should remain substantially lower than Mini, who is 57% rostered.

articles.title: Inside Taylor Townsend’s emotional journey from adversity to another US Open run, shaped by motherhood and resilience
articles.summary: International Sports News: Taylor Townsend’s 2026 US Open run ended with a 6-4, 6-3 loss to World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka, but the American still leaves New York with another stro.
articles.body: Taylor Townsend’s 2026 US Open run ended with a 6-4, 6-3 loss to World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka, but the American still leaves New York with another strong singles showing. The 30-year-old reached the fourth round for the second straight year after beating Diana Shnaider in three sets. Before facing Sabalenka, Townsend had also produced one of the best serving performances of her career, winning all 23 first-serve points against Taylah Preston. Her latest run is another part of a career shaped by setbacks, motherhood and a major rise in doubles.Taylor Townsend built a different path after becoming a motherTownsend’s career has never followed a simple route. She made headlines as a teenager, but her progress was affected by difficult experiences away from the court. She has also spoken about problems involving her early earnings and how those experiences changed the way she handled her career.Motherhood later became another major part of her story. Townsend gave birth to her son, Adyn Aubrey, in March 2021 and returned to competition the following year. Since then, she has continued to compete at the highest level while balancing professional tennis with raising her son.Rather than seeing motherhood as the end of her career, Townsend has treated it as part of her motivation. She has also spoken about wanting her son to have a different experience from some of the things she went through as a child.Her doubles career has been especially successful. Townsend became the WTA’s No. 1 doubles player in July 2025 and has won five doubles titles, including Grand Slam success. She is currently No. 2 in the doubles rankings and is coached by Roger Tyzzer.That success has helped Townsend build confidence in singles too. At this year’s US Open, her serve became one of the biggest strengths of her game. Against Preston, she won every point behind her first serve and hit eight aces. Afterward, she joked about whether she had become a “servebot.”“I don’t know. I think they call this a ‘servebot.’ Am I a servebot now? Maybe.”She then credited Reilly Opelka with helping popularize the term among tennis fans.Taylor Townsend continues to write her own tennis storyTownsend’s fourth-round appearance also added to a growing list of memorable US Open moments. She famously defeated then-World No. 4 Simona Halep at the 2019 tournament and reached the fourth round again this year after beating Shnaider 6-2, 6-7(3), 6-3.Against Sabalenka, Townsend had to deal with a completely different challenge. The defending champion and world No. 1 used her power and consistency to win in straight sets and move into the quarterfinals.Still, Townsend’s tournament showed how far her singles game has come. Her aggressive return position, left-handed serve and willingness to move forward make her uncomfortable for opponents, while her doubles experience has given her another advantage at the net.The result against Sabalenka ended this year’s singles campaign in New York, but it did not erase what Townsend had already achieved. She reached the fourth round at a Grand Slam again while continuing to compete as one of the world’s best doubles players.For Townsend, that is another step in a career she has built on her own terms. Her story now includes elite doubles success, motherhood and a renewed singles run - all after years in which many people were unsure where her career would go.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Team GB&I storms back to shock the U.S. and win the Walker Cup
articles.summary: Team Great Britain & Ireland won seven of 10 points during Sunday Singles to complete an improbable Walker Cup comeback.
articles.body:
Team Great Britain and Ireland are Walker Cup champions once again — and they did so in improbable fashion.

Entering the final singles session on Sunday afternoon at Lahinch Golf Club, Team USA looked to be on their way to a sixth consecutive victory in the biennial team competition as they held a 9.5 to 6.5 advantage. However, thanks to a historic final session that saw GB&I win seven of the available 10 points, the team from across the pond completed the comeback for a 13.5 to 12.5 victory.

"I believed in the team the whole time," said GB&I captain Dean Robertson. "I'm so proud of them. Just so special."

After Team USA swept the morning foursomes session, the three-point lead entering the final session looked all but insurmountable. Needing seven points in the final singles session, GB&I's margin for error was razor thin. Luckily, many of them saved their best golf for last.

GB&I swept the first four matches of the session — including a historic 8&7 beatdown in the third match courtesy of newly minted U.S. Amateur champ Jack Whaley — and went on to halve the fifth match as well. Suddenly, what looked like a sure Team USA waltz to victory transformed into a furious comeback bid.

"I mean, just said, look, I'm just going to go out there and have fun," said Luke Poulter, who won his match over Ethan Feng 3&1. "I was looking over at the leaderboard and I could see a bunch of blue on the board and that's all I wanted to see."

On the strength of sweeping the first four matches, GB&I found itself in the lead by a single point. Still with work to be done, the bottom half of the lineup fed off the momentum from earlier matches and continued the spirited surge.

In matches 5 and 7, Niall Sheils Donegan and Connor Graham were each able to earn a half point, with each tying the young Americans Miles Russell and Kihei Akina. Sandwiched between the halved matches, Eliot Baker earned a full point over Walker Cup veteran Stewart Hagestad with a birdie on the final hole.

With the GB&I tally pushed to 12.5, just a single point was all that separated them from breaking their Walker Cup drought. And that point would come courtesy of Josh Hill.

Facing off against American Tyler Watts, Hill found himself all square in his match as he played the finishing hole. Then, it what will go down in Walker Cup lore, Hill managed to card birdie on the par-5 finisher (aided by a spectacular bunker shot), officially pushing his team over the finish line to victory.

"It's unbelievable," Hill said. "Doesn't get better than this."

articles.title: Ex-Boston Celtics Star Isaiah Thomas Makes Announcement About Career
articles.summary: Isaiah Thomas is back with the Celtics organization, but the two-time All-Star made clear that he is not necessarily finished playing basketball. The post Ex...
articles.body:
Former Boston Celtics star Isaiah Thomas has begun preparing for life after his playing career, but the two-time NBA All-Star apparently isn't ready to close that chapter just yet.

Thomas, now 37 and working as a pro and college scout for the Celtics, declared on X on September 6 that he wants to spend a season playing outside the United States.

"I want to hoop overseas for a year!!! I want that experience! And to cook them boys over that water," Thomas wrote.

It wasn't his only post suggesting that his competitive fire remains intact. Thomas later wrote , "Take this SLOW GRIND to another country and go crazy!!!!!!!!"

The comments are notable because Thomas only recently returned to Boston in an official capacity, nearly nine years after his memorable run as the Celtics' star point guard ended.

Isaiah Thomas Isn't Completely Ready to Stop Playing

Thomas' new role with Boston appeared to signal the beginning of his post-playing career.

The Celtics hired Thomas as a pro and college scout in May, with The Boston Globe's Adam Himmelsbach reporting that Thomas would primarily work from his hometown of Seattle and help Boston evaluate players on the West Coast.

Thomas even participated in Boston's draft process this summer. Celtics assistant general manager Mike Zarren said Thomas was the person who called the team's Dillon Mitchell selection into the NBA during the 2026 draft.

But Thomas acknowledged shortly after accepting the job that moving away from the court wasn't easy.

"This has not been the easiest transition, first and foremost, because I can still play at a high level," Thomas said on his "Point Game" podcast in May .

Thomas isn't simply reminiscing about playing. He is publicly floating a specific next step — spending a season overseas — while simultaneously beginning a possible long-term career in an NBA front office.

There is no indication yet that Thomas has signed with an international club or is negotiating with one. His post should therefore be viewed as an expression of what he wants to do rather than confirmation that an overseas season is happening.

Thomas Has Continued Chasing Another Playing Opportunity

Thomas' determination to continue playing isn't particularly surprising considering how aggressively he has pursued opportunities in recent years.

His most recent NBA stint came with the Phoenix Suns late in the 2023-24 season. Thomas appeared in six regular-season games for Phoenix.

Thomas returned to the Salt Lake City Stars, the Utah Jazz's G League affiliate, in January 2025. The Stars noted that Thomas had averaged 32.5 points, 5.3 assists and 3.0 rebounds over four G League appearances during his previous stint with the club in 2024.

An overseas move would represent something different. Thomas has spent his professional career pursuing NBA opportunities rather than playing internationally, and Eurohoops reported on September 6 that he has previously been connected to EuroLeague possibilities without making the move.

Isaiah Thomas' Celtics Peak Remains His Career High Point

Thomas' connection to Boston makes his next move particularly interesting for Celtics fans.

The 5-foot-9 guard became one of the NBA's biggest stars during the 2016-17 season, averaging a career-best 28.9 points and 5.9 assists while helping Boston reach the Eastern Conference Finals. He earned All-NBA Second Team honors that year.

Boston traded Thomas to the Cleveland Cavaliers in August 2017 as the centerpiece of the deal for Kyrie Irving. His career was subsequently disrupted by hip issues, and he never again reached the level he had established with the Celtics.

Nearly a decade later, Thomas has finally made his way back into Boston's organization.

His latest comments suggest that reunion does not necessarily mean his playing days are over.

For now, Thomas may be helping the Celtics identify their next players. He also seems determined to prove he can still be one himself.

articles.title: Ex-Browns QB Gets $13 Million Payday
articles.summary: The former Cleveland Browns quarterback just secured his future. The post Ex-Browns QB Gets $13 Million Payday appeared first on HEAVY.
articles.body:
Jameis Winston has built an NFL career around keeping everyone guessing. The New York Giants have seen enough to make one thing certain: They want him sticking around.

Former Cleveland Browns quarterback Winston earned a two-year, $13 million extension with the Giants, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz.

Winston appeared in three games for the Giants last season, making two starts while Jaxson Dart was sidelined with a concussion. He completed 37 of 66 passes for 567 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions.

The Giants lost both of Winston's starts, but the offense remained competitive. New York averaged 23.5 points against the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions, with Winston taking only three sacks. He also rushed for a touchdown and caught a 33-yard score on a trick play.

His best showing came against Detroit, when he passed for 366 yards and two touchdowns in a 34-27 overtime loss.

Jameis Winston Delivered Wild Ride With Browns

There were always two sides to a Winston start during his brief tenure in Cleveland. He could energize an offense, attack downfield and produce stretches of explosive football. He could also take unnecessary chances and turn a competitive game with a costly mistake.

Winston signed a one-year, $4 million contract with the Browns in 2024 and initially backed up Deshaun Watson. He moved into the starting lineup after Watson ruptured his Achilles in October.

His first start delivered one of the brightest moments of Cleveland's three-win season. Winston threw for 334 yards and three touchdowns in a 29-24 upset of the Baltimore Ravens , earning AFC Offensive Player of the Week honors. He also helped Cleveland beat the Pittsburgh Steelers during a memorable Thursday night snow game.

The full Winston experience arrived against the Denver Broncos . He set a Browns single-game record with 497 passing yards and threw four touchdowns. However, he also tossed three interceptions, including two returned for touchdowns, in a 41-32 loss.

Winston finished his Browns tenure with 2,121 passing yards, 13 touchdowns and 12 interceptions. He went 2-5 as the starter and threw eight interceptions over his final three starts before being benched for Dorian Thompson-Robinson.

The Browns allowed Winston to leave in free agency, and he signed his original two-year, $8 million deal with New York in March 2025.

Browns Still Searching for Quarterback Stability

Winston has secured his place in New York, but the Browns remain without a definitive long-term answer at quarterback. Todd Monken named Watson the Week 1 starter following a competition with Shedeur Sanders. Watson has not appeared in a regular-season game since October 2024.

He is 9-10 over 19 starts with Cleveland and has not played more than seven games in any season since signing his fully guaranteed $230 million contract.

Sanders will open the season as the primary backup after starting seven games as a rookie. He completed 56.6% of his passes for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions last season.

Rookie Taylen Green is the third quarterback, while Dillon Gabriel will begin the year on injured reserve because of a back injury.

articles.title: Chivas and a Showcase of Their Resources in San Luis Potosí
articles.summary: Guadalajara defeated Atlético de San Luis 0-3 in Jornada 7 of the Apertura 2026, showcasing their efficiency, pressing and ability to adapt, once again highl...
articles.body:
Guadalajara defeated Atlético de San Luis 0-3 in Jornada 7 of the Apertura 2026, showcasing their efficiency, pressing and ability to adapt, once again highlighting the wealth of resources available to Gabriel Milito's side. Some matches are won by a single detail. Others, by an individual moment of brilliance. And then there are performances like Chivas' in San Luis, in which the final score is merely a reflection of a dominant display built across different phases of the game.

The 0-3 victory at Estadio Alfonso Lastras was a snapshot of what Guadalajara can offer when its players execute the game plan correctly. High pressing, clean buildup from the back, the ability to pin down the opposition's defensive line and, above all, excellent decision-making from the bench to change the course of the match when Atlético de San Luis attempted to react.

One of Guadalajara's main strengths was their pressing. Chivas constantly disrupted San Luis' buildup and, through that work, recovered possession in areas that allowed them to attack with an advantage. The defensive structure also underwent an important adjustment with the return of Daniel Aguirre, who operated as a right-sided stopper and gave the team a cleaner outlet from the back.

Hugo Camberos and Roberto Alvarado did not have to cover large distances as wing-backs. Both played much higher up the pitch, almost as wingers, allowing Chivas to have a greater presence and width in the opposition half. And when the match began to become more difficult to break open, another quality emerged: the ability to change players' roles without completely altering the structure.

Alvarado began to drop deeper in the buildup, getting closer to the first passes and helping maintain possession. 'Piojo' was not only influential in the opposition half; he also became an important outlet for playing out from the back.

Three Forwards Against Three Center Backs

The opening goal perfectly summarized one of Gabriel Milito's main intentions for the match: creating a three-versus-three situation against Atlético de San Luis' center backs. Ángel Sepúlveda, Ricardo Marín and Santiago Sandoval were responsible for pinning down the home side's defensive line. Sandoval, who essentially operated as a third forward, perfectly read the space that opened up between the center backs and arrived there to finish and make it 0-1.

It was not an isolated play. It was the consequence of an idea.

Chivas managed to give the home defenders clear references on the rojiblancos attackers while simultaneously finding spaces to attack between the lines. The second goal once again showcased that same intention.

Sepúlveda received the ball with his marker practically attached to him, but used his body to protect possession before laying it off first-time to Ricardo Marín. The rojiblanco forward took advantage of the play and produced an excellent finish to extend the lead. Two goals, two examples of how Guadalajara managed to maximize the characteristics of their forwards.

Atlético de San Luis changed their approach in the second half. The home side came out with greater aggression, took control of possession and, for several minutes, managed to push the match into rojiblanco territory. Chivas lost some of their control and the scenario looked different from the first half.

That was when another of Guadalajara's great strengths emerged: their ability to adjust.

Gabriel Milito moved two pieces and found his way back into the match. Efraín Álvarez's introduction gave the team a player capable of staying wide on the left while also moving inside. Kevin Castañeda came on to add a presence between the lines and behind San Luis' midfielders, while Chivas sacrificed a forward to gain an extra player in that area.

The effect was immediate. Guadalajara once again found better connections and regained control of the ball. Even the first passes began to come from players we usually think of as attackers. Alvarado and Álvarez participated from deeper areas, offering passing lanes and helping build attacks from the back.

That detail is important: Chivas did not rely solely on their center backs or midfielders to initiate their attacks. Their own forwards were capable of becoming playmakers.

The Third, Another Display of Combination Play

The 0-3 scoreline ultimately completed the showcase. Ricardo Marín once again played with his back to goal, held off his marker and laid the ball off precisely to Richard Ledezma, who found himself facing goal and unleashed a powerful shot that beat the San Luis goalkeeper.

The combination once again highlighted one of the defining characteristics of this Guadalajara side: the ability to create advantages through short combinations, movement and players capable of interpreting different roles.

Ledezma, in addition, enjoyed an excellent spell after coming on down the right wing. His involvement provided freshness and depth during the final stages of the match.

The victory in San Luis is valuable for the three points, but also for everything it tells us about this Chivas side. Guadalajara was able to press, build, pin the opposition back, attack spaces, change their positioning and respond when the opponent changed their approach. They were a team that found solutions both through the initial structure and from the bench. And that speaks volumes about the number of resources available to Gabriel Milito.

Guadalajara showed that they can control a match in different ways. They can do it through high pressing, positional attacks, direct play toward their forwards or by creating numerical advantages between the lines.

On a difficult pitch, the Rebaño delivered a complete performance and secured a convincing 0-3 victory that allowed them to climb the standings.

Chivas has the resources. Milito has the alternatives. And San Luis was yet another example of that.

articles.title: What's at stake when the Chicago Cubs face the Brewers this week?
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs are in town to face Milwaukee for three games; just how crucial are those games in the playoff picture?
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers didn't exactly cloak themselves in glory during a 3-4 stretch against the Chicago Cubs and Cincinnati Reds last week, but with the same teams heading into American Family Field (starting Sept. 7), the Brewers' eight-game lead in the Central heading into last week has only been trimmed to seven.

The Brewers only really need to stave off a sweep at the hands of the Cubs to still feel comfortable with their division lead heading into the weekend; even one win should keep things relatively calm. The Brewers could easily clinch a playoff spot on the homestand, although it won't be the first two days against the Cubs.

The division will probably have to wait until the Brewers' final road trip.

Here's what to know about the three-game series against Chicago that begins on Labor Day.

Who's pitching in the series between the Brewers and Cubs?

All three games will air on Brewers.TV and AM-620 WTMJ radio. The game will also air on FOX on Tuesday.

Sept. 7, 1:10 p.m.: Milwaukee LHP Robert Gasser (4-5, 4.57) vs. Chicago LHP Matthew Boyd (8-3, 4.05).

Sept. 8, 6:40 p.m.: Milwaukee RHP Jacob Misiorowski (14-5, 1.97) vs. Chicago LHP David Peterson (7-8, 5.39).

Sept. 8, 6:40 p.m.: Milwaukee RHP Logan Henderson (9-3, 2.48) vs. Chicago RHP Kevin Gausman (9-11, 4.38).

Didn't the Brewers just see these three Cubs pitchers?

They sure did. A lot will feel the same this week with the Cubs and Reds back on the calendar for six games at American Family Field after the Brewers played on the road against those teams this past week. The Brewers won't see Clay Holmes, who held them in check during a 17-3 shellacking, but did do enough against Boyd and Peterson to secure wins (with a little help from the Cubs bullpen).

Henderson and Gausman will rematch after Gausman and his split-finger fastball flummoxed the Brewers in a 2-1 loss Thursday. The Brewers got to Boyd for three runs in 5⅓ innings and tagged Peterson for six in 3⅔.

Can the Brewers clinch a playoff spot during the series?

Yes, but it requires a lot to go right. The Brewers magic number to secure a playoff spot is seven, with the Diamondbacks and Padres straddling the final wild-card spot in the National League with 68 losses each. Those two have a three-game series against each other still on the schedule later in September, so we know one of them will get at least two more losses. That means the magic number is really five right now (since the Brewers have to only finish ahead of one of them to lock up a playoff spot).

The Brewers have the tiebreaker over the Diamondbacks and do not against the Padres, so the head-to-head number for the Brewers to officially finish better than Arizona is 6 and San Diego is 7.

Easiest path? Brewers sweep the Cubs, knocking three off the magic number and the Diamondbacks lose all three games at Kansas City, knocking the other three off. The best Arizona can do after that scenario is tie the Brewers at the end of the year, and the Brewers would have the tiebreaker.

Another scenario would involve the Brewers winning all three games and both San Diego and Arizona losing two of three (the Padres face Washington). Then, the Brewers would be in because their magic number to "eliminate" either one of them would be two, and the Brewers know one of them is guaranteed to lose twice more, so it's a done deal even if they don't know which team is the one "eliminated."

The last scenario would be Arizona and San Diego both getting swept and the Brewers winning two of three. We're in the same place as above, where the magic number is two but one of them is getting two more losses eventually to account for the final slashes off the magic number.

How early can the Brewers win the division?

A sweep against the Cubs would really help and account for half of the remaining 12 on the magic number tally. The Brewers would still be able to secure the Central by the end of the homestand on Sunday, but it requires nearly everything to go right. It's far more likely it happens on the upcoming three-city road trip to Pittsburgh, Baltimore and Philadelphia.

What do the Brewers need to do to get the tiebreaker over the Cubs?

Milwaukee needs to win just one game to lock up the season series and hold the tiebreaker. Thus, while the magic number is 12 heading into the week, a win Monday would actually slice that down to 9, since the goal is no longer to finish with an outright better record; a tie will do. The Brewers are 6-4 against the Cubs this year and need to get to seven wins in the 13-game season series.

The Cubs just won a series in Miami after splitting four games against the Brewers at Wrigley Field, but the Cubs had lost four of five series prior to that, and the one win over the White Sox required two walk-off victories. The Brewers have been scuffling a bit in the past few weeks, but they're still 12-8 over their last 20 games, while the Cubs are 9-11.

Pete Crow-Armstrong has been a behemoth against everyone else but quiet against Milwaukee

With his 40th home run on Sept. 6, outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong is one step closer to winning the National League MVP award, especially with Shohei Ohtani ailing and seemingly unlikely to pitch the rest of the way. The defensive wizard center fielder PCA has a .946 OPS this year, with 33 stolen bases and 96 RBIs.

The funny thing is, Brewers fans haven't seen the best of PCA. Though he did hit a tough Logan Henderson pitch out to center field to account for Chicago's runs in a 2-1 win Thursday, it's his only extra-base hit against the Brewers this year in 10 games. He's batting 4 for 37 (.108) this season against Milwaukee. In his career, it's a .164 batting average and .620 OPS.

Either the Brewers know the best way to attack Crow-Armstrong or he's due.

Much has been made about how bad the Chicago Cubs bullpen has been lately, and it hasn't been dazzling. The Cubs have a 5.16 ERA since Aug. 20, though five teams in MLB have been worse, and Cincinnati, the other team in Milwaukee's recent orbit, has a 5.12 ERA. In the small sample since September started, the Cubs aren't even in the bottom third in bullpen ERA.

For the year, Chicago's 3.98 ERA is 12th best in baseball. You know who has been good out of the Cubs bullpen in longer relief? Aaron Civale.

articles.title: WWE Sunday Night's Main Event 2026 Live Updates, Results and Highlights
articles.summary: Welcome to Bleacher Report's live coverage of Sunday Night's Main Event on September 6. Keep it locked right here for live updates from throughout the show at the State Farm Arena in Atlanta, Georgia.
articles.body:
Welcome to Bleacher Report's live coverage of Sunday Night's Main Event on September 6. Keep it locked right here for live updates from throughout the show at the State Farm Arena in Atlanta, Georgia.

Rhodes looked confused as he realized what had happened. The show ended with Orton looking bloody and not very satisfied with his victory.

Orton was bleeding from his ear as Rhodes rolled him back into the ring. He hit a super Cody Cutter, but there still wasn't a ref to count the pin.

The American Nightmare hit two Cross Rhodes in a row, and then he seemed to rethink his strategy. He looked down at a bloody Viper with a smile and lined up for the Punt Kick.

Orton begged for mercy, which caused Cody to stop. He looked conflicted about what to do as a new ref arrived to check on Orton. The Viper hit a low blow to both Rhodes and the referee at the same time.

He grabbed Cody and hit the RKO as the original ref climbed back into the ring to count the pin.

Orton hit the draping DDT and signaled for the RKO as the crowd gave him a combination of cheers and boos. Cody countered the RKO and hit Cross Rhodes, but it only got him a two-count.

Rhodes ended up colliding with the official, so when Orton hit the RKO, there was nobody to make the count. The Legend Killer got that look in his eye and backed up for the Punt Kick.

Rhodes avoided the kick and hit Cross Rhodes. Randy rolled out of the ring, so Cody hit a suicide dive that ended up taking out the referee again because he was behind Orton when he got hit.

The American Nightmare slammed Orton's head into the ring post several times and yelled at him as he hit him repeatedly with punches. He picked up the steel steps and hit The Viper in the face with them.

As soon as the bell rang, Rhodes hit a Cody Cutter and then put Orton in a Figure Four, but The Viper made it to the bottom rope to force a break. Orton took control and choked Cody against the middle rope. He slowed things down and started taking The American Nightmare apart piece by piece.

Rhodes began to mount some offense and sent Orton over the top rope, but when he tried to follow, Randy poked him in the eye. Every time Cody tried to take control, Orton seemed to have a counter for him.

Brandi ended up throwing a drink in Orton's face before Cody started fighting back. He hit a snap powerslam, followed by the Disaster Kick. He hit the Dusty Bionic Elbow, but The Viper countered Cross Rhodes.

Rhodes was out first for the main event. He wore a black skull mask with red wings for his entrance. When it was time for Orton's entrance, he tried to sneak attack Cody from behind, but he got caught.

Rhodes went out of the ring and started beating on him. He sent Randy over the barricade into the crowd. The match hadn't even started yet, but they were fighting all over the arena.

They continued to brawl throughout the crowd as fans chanted Orton's name. The Viper taunted Brandi Rhodes in the front row before they finally got into the ring so the match could officially get started.

Joe Tessitore and The Miz were serving as hosts between segments. They talked about the return of Bronson Reed and how many Tsunamis he hit on Femi.

All that is left on the card is Rhodes vs. Orton in a grudge match.

Jade and the Baddies vs. Flair, Bliss and Paxley Part 2

The Baddies kept Bliss away from her corner for a long time while double and triple-teaming her. Bliss hit a strange move that sent B-Fab into the corner and allowed her to make the hot tag to Charlotte.

The Queen unloaded on Michin with chops and hit a nice release German suplex. Flair maintained the upper hand, but Cargill made a blind tag and took her out with a kick to the face.

She lifted Charlotte onto her shoulders for a spinning Sandstorm, but Tatum broke it up at the last moment. Flair put Michin and Jade next to each other so she could hit a moonsault on both at the same time, but it only got her a two-count.

B-Fab dispatched Bliss by sending her into the steps. Cargill was able to get the win by pinning Flair with Jaded after her and Paxley's heads collided.

Jade and The Baddies vs. Flair, Bliss and Paxley Part 1

T-Pain was shown sitting in the crowd before we went backstage to see Heyman getting angry while talking to someone on the phone. Back in the arena, The Queen made her entrance for the six-woman tag match. Kelly Kelly's titantron was shown for a moment during Paxley's entrance.

Tatum and B-Fab started with a basic lockup. B-Fab talked some trash, but it didn't faze the former NXT champion. She unloaded on B-Fab and hit a rolling kick to the back of the head for a two-count.

She was able to fight off Michin, too, but Cargill attacked her at ringside to give her team the upper hand. The Baddies isolated Paxley for a moment, but she eventually tagged Bliss in to take over.

She almost hit Sister Abigail, but Michin saved B-Fab and allowed her to take control again.

Up next, Jade Cargill, B-Fab and Michin will take on Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley.

Breakker had to resort to raking the eyes to escape Femi's grasp, but when he tried to run around the ring for a Spear, Femi laid him out. Austin Theory showed up and got slammed through the announce table, but the distraction allowed Bron to hit the Spear.

He rolled Oba back in the ring and hit a second Spear, but it still wasn't enough to keep him down. Logan Paul showed up and the ref immediately ejected him, but it was just to distract the ref so Maxxine could sneak the brass knuckles to Bron.

As Femi was about to win, Bronson Reed made his return and attacked him with a steel chair.

Reed looked like he has dropped a lot of weight and is in the best shape of his career. He helped Breakker to his feet so he could hit another Spear to a defenseless Femi.

Reed hit the Tsunami a few times as officials tried to call him off.

Breakker began to build up a head of steam as he leapt from the apron and sent Femi over the announce table with a clothesline. When they brought the fight back into the ring, Bron hit a gutbuster for a two-count.

He started looking more confident and talked a lot of trash. Femi tried to fire back, but Breakker sent him out of the ring and drove his spine into the apron.

Oba broke out of a sleeper and started to fight back with big right hands. They traded shots until The Ruler started hitting clotheslines and uppercuts. He hit a chokeslam, but Breakker kicked out at two.

Paul Heyman was in the ring to give us an intro before the match. Once again, he hyped whoever wins as the future of WWE. He gave each Superstar an introduction in his signature style.

The bell rang and neither man moved. They stood there staring at each other for a moment before locking up. They fought for control, with Femi pushing Breakker to the corner to show off his power. Bron pushed him before locking up again. He pushed Oba to the opposite corner and began barking at him.

Breakker tried a shoulder tackle, but Femi didn't go down. When Bron tried to get a bigger running start, he ended up running into a brick wall and Femi sent him down to the mat.

Oba followed him out of the ring and dropped him onto the apron, but Breakker was able to send him into the ring post. He tried to run at Femi on the apron, and Femi hit him in the chest so hard that it echoed in the arena.

After Williams regained the U.S. title from Corbin, we went to the most anticipated match of the night between Oba Femi and Bron Breakker. It was shocking that this did not end up as the main event. It had the best build.

Corbin slowed the pace down and tossed Williams into the steel steps a couple of times. Trick tried to fight back, but one big clothesline put him right back down.

They ended up colliding with clotheslines at the same time to take each other out. Both men started taking shots at each other as they got back to their feet. Trick hit the Book End as he started to fire himself up, but he missed the Trick Shot and got hit with Deep Six, giving Corbin a near-fall.

He tried to bring the title into the ring, but Yachty held onto it. The distraction allowed Williams to hit a big spinning kick, but he only got a two-count.

Corbin used the belt behind the ref's back, but Trick managed to kick out at two. The Nomad went for his finisher, but Williams hit the Trick Shot for the pin and the win to regain his United States Championship.

WINNER: TRICK WILLIAMS WINS THE UNITED STATES CHAMPIONSHIP

As soon as Williams hit the ring, the ref called for the bell and he started taking it to the champion. He clotheslined Corbin out of the ring and slammed his head into the announce table a few times.

The champ sent Trick into the ring post and threw Yachty into the timekeeper's area. Trick Willy started to build some momentum when they got back into the ring. He hit a few of his signature moves as the crowd chanted for him.

He stomped The Nomad in the corner and hit a fireman's carry slam for a two-count. Corbin knocked him off the apron and into the announce table to regain control.

Yachty shocked the crowd by hitting a hurricanrana from the middle rope and a crossbody from the top rope, but it wasn't enough to get the pin.

Corbin hit the End of Days, but he saw he had 90 seconds left, so he decided to inflict more damage instead of going for the pin. He hit a second EOD with a minute left.

The Nomad brought a table into the ring and set it up with 30 seconds left on the clock. He put the musician on the top turnbuckle for a superplex, but Yachty countered and the clock ran out.

WINNER: LIL YACHTY SURVIVED FIVE MINUTES

And angry Corbin grabbed Yachty and chokeslammed him through the table as the announcer revealed Williams would get his title shot right now.

The stipulation for this match stated if Yachty could survive five minutes against Baron Corbin, then Trick Williams would earn a U.S. title shot. Corbin came out on a pretty nice motorcycle for his entrance.

Corbin grabbed a mic and gave Yachty one more chance to back out, but the rapper took a cheap shot and almost got the pin right away to kickstart the match. The Nomad chased him until he caught him and started throwing Yachty into the barricade.

Corbin took out a few members of Yachty's crew before the rapper found his kendo stick under the ring and started using it against him. At the halfway mark, Corbin wiped him out with a clothesline.

SNME opened with Quavo performing on the stage. When he was done, Lil Yachty and Trick Williams were shown preparing for their entrance backstage. Yachty had a whole entourage with him.

Sunday Night's Main Event is on the air! Michael Cole welcomed us to the show before we went to a video package hyping the show.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s $4.5 billion brand partnership adds another major win to her growing off-court empire and global influence
articles.summary: International Sports News: Caitlin Clark’s influence is stretching well beyond the basketball court. The Indiana Fever star has added another chapter to her growing business por.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark’s influence is stretching well beyond the basketball court. The Indiana Fever star has added another chapter to her growing business portfolio with a new Stanley 1913 collection, giving fans a fresh way to connect with one of the biggest names in women’s basketball. The collaboration also shows how Clark’s appeal continues to reach lifestyle audiences, with her athletic success and cultural impact making her a natural fit for major brands.Caitlin Clark expands her brand with Stanley 1913Clark and Stanley 1913 announced their latest collection this week, building on a partnership that first began in 2025. The collaboration combines Clark’s growing profile with Stanley’s strong presence in the drinkware market.The collection carries the Caitlin Clark Future design across several popular products. Fans can choose from a 40-ounce Quencher ProTour Flip Straw Tumbler priced at $55, a 30-ounce version for $45, a 24-ounce IceFlow Flip Straw 2.0 Bottle for $40 and a 24-ounce Vitalize Tempo Bottle priced at $45.Stanley positioned the collaboration around the idea of effort happening away from the spotlight."The quiet work speaks the loudest. The Stanley 1913 x @caitlinclark22 collection is available now on Stanley1913.com."The message fits neatly with Clark’s image. Her rise has been driven not only by game-day performances but also by the enormous attention surrounding women’s basketball. She has become one of the sport’s most recognizable figures, with her popularity creating opportunities that extend into fashion, fitness, food and lifestyle.Her Stanley partnership adds another piece to that picture.Clark already has a long list of major commercial relationships, including Nike, Gatorade, State Farm and Wilson. Her Nike agreement is particularly significant, reportedly worth $28 million over eight years, with a signature sneaker line forming a major part of the deal.Caitlin Clark’s Stanley partnership reflects her influenceStanley’s decision to continue working with Clark highlights how brands increasingly see women’s sports stars as more than athletes. Clark brings a large fan base, but her appeal also crosses into a wider culture that follows her personality, style and career.When the partnership was announced in 2025, Matt Navarro, global president of PMI WW Brands, LLC, praised Clark’s impact on basketball and beyond."It is an incredible honor to partner with a global sports icon like Caitlin Clark. She is redefining women's sports and reshaping culture through her drive, passion, and grit," Navarro said. "She's not just a leader in the world of basketball; she is sparking a global movement."Navarro described the original collaboration as a celebration of that influence and the people who share Clark’s determination to make an impact.Clark also explained why the partnership appealed to her."Partnering with Stanley 1913 is an exciting opportunity to work with a brand that shares my values and champions women's sports," Clark said in a statement. "This collection has something for everyone – from the athletes putting in the work on the court to the fans shaping the culture."That connection is important. Clark’s commercial success mirrors the broader growth of women’s sports, where star athletes are increasingly becoming powerful voices outside competition.For the Fever guard, every new partnership adds another layer to a brand that is still developing. Her basketball career remains the center of her public profile, but deals such as the Stanley collaboration show why companies are eager to associate themselves with her.The latest collection is therefore more than a lineup of tumblers and bottles. It is another sign of Clark’s expanding reach. From packed arenas to everyday lifestyle products, her name continues to travel far beyond the basketball court.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: WWE Sunday Night's Main Event Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights
articles.summary: WWE returned to Peacock for the first-ever Sunday Night's Main Event special, headlined by a WrestleMania 42 rematch between Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton.
articles.body:
WWE returned to Peacock for the first-ever Sunday Night's Main Event special, headlined by a WrestleMania 42 rematch between Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton.

That match headlined a jam-packed card that could have doubled as a live event special, at least on paper.

Did the card deliver, and how did each match grade out?

Find out the answers to those questions and more in this recap of the primetime special.

Announced in advance of Sunday's show were:

Charlotte Flair, Tatum Paxley, and Alexa Bliss vs. Jade Cargill, B-Fab, and Michin

Last Time in Action: Baron Corbin defeated Carmelo Hayes (SmackDown, August 14); Lil Yachty has never wrestled a WWE match

Played to the ring by his fellow rap superstar, Quavo, Lil Yachty took to the squared circle Sunday night with one goal in mind: last five minutes in the ring with United States Champion Baron Corbin to earn Trick Williams a United States Championship Match.

Corbin predictably steamrolled Yachty, outside of a few teases of offense for the underdog, and had him beaten more than once. His hubris got the best of him, though, and Yachty crotched him on the top rope as time expired, passing the test.

The Nomad responded by chokeslamming him through a table in time for Williams to hit the ring for his title opportunity.

Lil Yachty survived the five-minute time limit

This was exactly what it needed to be. Yachty showed enough to keep the fans invested and Corbin's arrogance cost him. The match was a lot of fun and the crowd was red-hot for all of it.

Corbin is, and has been, criminally underrated by fans for so long that performances like this, where he worked his ass off to sell the story against an untrained rapper, fly under the radar. He was great here in what served as further evidence of why management trusts him to walk back in the door and win a title right away.

United States Championship Match: Trick Williams vs. Baron Corbin

Last Time in Action: Trick Williams lost to Baron Corbin (SmackDown, August 7); Corbin lost to Lil Yachty (Sunday Night's Main Event, September 6)

Still smarting from the humiliation of failing to defeat Lil Yachty in five minutes, Corbin faced the unenviable task of immediately defending his United States Championship against Williams.

He weathered the storm early, worked over Williams to the midway point, and survived a late-match cyclone boot by kicking out at the last possible second.

Williams regained the United States Championship in a molten-hot match that saw him survive a shot to the face with the title belt, then rock Corbin with a Trick Shot to secure the win and his second reign with the gold.

Williams defeated Corbin to win the title

Williams and Corbin have deceptively strong in-ring chemistry. The match at SummerSlam may have underwhelmed but the rematch on SmackDown last month and this were exponentially better. This was a fantastic match that played on spots from their previous encounters and the crowd erupted for Williams regaining the gold.

Does Corbin quietly move out of the championship picture or hang around? One would think they have accomplished all they could with the Williams-Corbin story for now, so perhaps it would be best for him to graduate to the WWE title picture, after the company wraps up the five-way feud currently ongoing.

Last Time In Action: Oba Femi defeated Brock Lesnar (SummerSlam, August 2); Bron Breakker defeated Joe Hendry (Raw, August 3)

Paul Heyman introduced the battle for WWE's future between Oba Femi and Bron Breakker, and both men shined in a hard-hitting, physical battle.

The Ruler dominated early, overwhelming The Badass often and leaving him reeling. The second-generation star fought his way back into the match, taking Femi over the announce table and mounting a comeback that saw him showcase his own strength and fury.

Late in the match, Femi survived a spear, sent Austin Theory sailing through the commentary table, and withstood an attempted brass knuckle shot following interference from Logan Paul and Maxxine Dupri.

As he prepared for the victory, though, Femi caught a nasty chair shot to the back from the returning Bronson Reed. The Auszilla delivered three Tsunamis to Femi, split only by a pair of spears from Breakker.

One last Tsunami from Reed put a bow on the heels' beatdown of The Ruler while also serving as a message to the rest of the Raw locker room that The Vision is still very much a threat.

Femi defeated Breakker via disqualification

Femi blasted Breakker with a chop to the chest on the ring apron that sounded like a rifle shot. It was an extraordinary visual and audio moment.

Theory continued to be the rag doll for The Vision, taking the big bumps that the others in the group either will not or cannot at this point. His flat-back bump through the commentary table made for a fun moment late.

This match was exactly what it needed to be: physical warfare featuring two young stars vying to be the guy moving forward, with a surprise return to propel the story forward. Reed looked great, here, so much so that he may have actually overshadowed Breakker in the closing minutes of the segment.

Last Time in Action: Charlotte Flair and Tatum Paxley defeated Fallon Henley and Lainey Reid (SmackDown, September 4); Alexa Bliss lost to Jade Cargill (SmackDown, July 10); Jade Cargill lost to Flair (SmackDown, August 7); B-Fab and Michin defeated Tiffany Stratton and Chelsea Green (SmackDown, July 31)

The ongoing rivalry between Jade Cargil and Charlotte Flair, and their many associates, wrote its latest chapter Sunday night in Atlanta in a Six-Woman Tag Team Match pitting The Queen, Bliss, and Paxley against The Storm, Michin, and B-Fab.

The action was wild and chaotic down the stretch, with Flair and Cargill starring late. As Paxley attempted to join Flair in a stereo Figure Four, B-Fab kicked her off, sending her headfirst into The Queen.

Cargill capitalized, drove Flair to the mat with Jaded, and scored the win in front of her fans and friends.

Cargill, B-Fab, and Michin defeated Flair, Paxley, and Bliss

There was a lot of action in this one but it broke down late in the contest before the finish. It was perfectly acceptable wrestling, but it very much feels like this feud is on a treadmill, with Paxley providing the only real update in recent months.

Speaking of Paxley, she has seamlessly transitioned to the main roster and if the reaction for her entrance was any indication, she figures to be a big fixture in the women's division.

Last Time in Action: Cody Rhodes lost to CM Punk (SummerSlam, August 2); Randy Orton lost to Rhodes (WrestleMania, April 18)

The Viper attempted to slither his way into the ring and attack The American Nightmare from behind before the bell Sunday night, but failed as Rhodes was ready for him.

The fight spilled into the stands as Rhodes punished Orton, showing the intensity and aggression he teased Friday on SmackDown. It did not change as the match returned to the squared circle and finally got underway.

Orton turned the tide in his favor and systematically picked apart Rhodes, grounding him and working over his former protege. At ringside, she slammed the former WWE champion into the commentary table, further punishing him. A momentary lapse, though, led to him confronting Brandi Rhodes at ringside and absorbing a drink to the face as a result.

Still, he recovered, cut off Cody's flurry of offense, and downed him with a big powerslam. The American Nightmare delivered the Cross Rhodes for two.

Orton finally caught Rhodes with an RKO, but only after referee Charles Robinson took a big bump.

Rhodes recovered and blasted Orton with the ring steps, busting him open. Back in the ring, the unhinged babyface delivered a super cutter, then added three Cross Rhodes. He set up for a punt that would have put Orton down, but the future Hall of Famer begged off and Rhodes gave him the mercy he asked for.

A cheap low blow to both Rhodes and replacement referee Eddie Orengo, followed by an RKO by Orton, earned the Legend Killer the victory.

This was the Rhodes we have needed to see for months. He was excellent here, aggressive and punishing. He was relentless, until he was not, and lost because of his momentary hesitation.

Orton resorting to groveling like a proper heel showed a new side of him, too, as he resorted to the most pathetic display. Yes, it benefited him, but it suggested we may be seeing a new side of the third-generation star, too.

Corbin was tasked with carrying the first 30 minutes of this year's show, and he succeeded spectacularly.

Not only was he fantastic in the five-minute sprint against a non-wrestler in Lil Yachty, but he also had a really fun title defense against Trick Williams. He did not leave Atlanta with the gold, but he was fantastic and made his case for a bigger role on SmackDown.

The first hour of Sunday's show was great, with the US title drama and the Oba Femi-Bron Breakker match. The back half was so-so, with an OK women's tag match and a Cody Rhodes-Randy Orton match that was really strong for two-thirds of it before falling off the rails with some unneeded overbooking.

articles.title: Trick Williams Wins WWE US Title After Lil Yachty 'Survives' vs. Baron Corbin at SNME
articles.summary: Lil Yachty made it five minutes without getting beaten by Baron Corbin at WWE Sunday Night's Main Event, and Trick Williams promptly defeated Corbin, making him the United States Champion.
articles.body:
Lil Yachty made it five minutes without getting beaten by Baron Corbin at WWE Sunday Night's Main Event, and Trick Williams promptly defeated Corbin, making him the United States Champion.

Live Sunday Night's Main Event Updates 📝

Corbin's rivalry with Trick and Yachty dates back to the July 10 episode of SmackDown, which saw Corbin make his WWE return after nearly two years away.

He interrupted a U.S. title match between Williams and Carmelo Hayes by attacking both of them, and that was enough to earn Corbin a title opportunity at SummerSlam.

Thanks in part to throwing Trick off his game by putting Yachty through a table, Corbin managed to upset Williams and become a two-time United States champion in the process.

Williams immediately went to work at trying to secure a rematch, but Corbin wasn't willing to hand one out unless he was able to dictate some of the terms.

After Yachty attacked Corbin with the Trick Stick kendo stick on a couple of occasions, Corbin devised a plan that would finally allow him to get his hands on the popular rapper.

Corbin proposed a match between him and Yachty with a five-minute time limit for Sunday Night's Main Event in Yachty's hometown of Atlanta.

He noted that if Yachty could avoid getting pinned or submitted for five minutes, then Trick would get a rematch. However, if Corbin could beat Yachty in the allotted time, Williams would not be permitted to challenge him for the U.S. title again.

Despite the size and strength disparity between Corbin and Yachty, Trick agreed to the stipulation and put his faith in his manager and friend.

That proved to be the right move, as Yachty showed his toughness and resilience by lasting five minutes in the ring with Corbin and securing Williams another shot at the United States Championship—and ultimately the belt.

articles.title: Oba Femi Beats Bron Breakker by DQ as Bronson Reed Returns at WWE SNME After Lesnar's Retirement
articles.summary: Coming off his SummerSlam victory over Brock Lesnar, Oba Femi defeated Bron Breakker at WWE Sunday Night's Main Event after Bronson Reed made a surprising return to the ring that led to Breakker's disqualification.
articles.body:
Coming off his SummerSlam victory over Brock Lesnar, Oba Femi defeated Bron Breakker at WWE Sunday Night's Main Event after Bronson Reed made a surprising return to the ring that led to Breakker's disqualification.

Femi's reward for the win was a massive beatdown following the bell.

After splitting his first two meetings with Lesnar at WrestleMania 42 and Clash in Italy, Femi scored arguably the biggest win of his career at SummerSlam, beating Lesnar in a Hell in a Cell match.

Lesnar announced his retirement shortly thereafter, and Paul Heyman was highly complimentary of Oba and his future prospects in WWE coming out of SummerSlam.

That didn't sit well with Breakker, who was once viewed as the future of WWE by Heyman, particularly when he first joined The Vision alongside Seth Rollins.

However, with Rollins long gone from the group and Lesnar returning to the mix at the time, Heyman seemingly lost interest in The Vision and ceased being as closely involved with the group as he once was.

That, coupled with Heyman showing immense respect for Femi, seemingly caused Breakker to question whether Heyman still viewed him in the same light as he used to.

That led to a segment on Raw a few weeks ago, which saw Femi and Breakker come face to face with Heyman serving as a mediator of sorts.

The Ruler mocked Breakker for incessantly pestering Heyman about his opinion on the true future of WWE, prompting Heyman to propose a match between them for Sunday Night's Main Event in Breakker's hometown of Atlanta.

After the match was made official, Breakker seemed satisfied and shook hands with Femi, but he was taken aback when Heyman shook Oba's hand as well.

Breakker was out to make a statement at Sunday Night's Main Event, but Femi stopped him in his tracks and continued to build momentum toward a potential future world title opportunity.

Jade Cargill, Michin and B-Fab beat Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley in a six-woman tag team match at WWE Sunday Night's Main Event.

During a singles match between Charlotte and Jade, both Michin and B-Fab kept getting involved, leading to the surprise main roster debut of Paxley, who evened the odds.

Flair took advantage by pinning Cargill to win the match, and the duo of Charlotte and Alexa officially became a trio with Tatum entering the fray.

Bliss revealed that it was her idea to bring Paxley into the fold, and although Flair was a bit unsure given Paxley's unique personality, there is no doubting her impressive résumé.

During Paxley's time in NXT from 2021 to 2026, she was a one-time NXT women's champion and women's North American champion, proving that her methods were successful.

While Flair and Bliss weren't quite sure what to expect out of Paxley because of her unpredictability, the same went for the triumvirate of Cargill, Michin and B-Fab.

Tatum helped her squad enter Sunday Night's Main Event with some momentum on their side by virtue of her singles victory over Michin on the Aug. 28 edition of SmackDown.

articles.title: Randy Orton Beats Cody Rhodes in WrestleMania Rematch at WWE SNME
articles.summary: In a rematch of their WrestleMania 42 Night 1 main event, Randy Orton defeated Cody Rhodes at WWE Sunday Night's Main Event.
articles.body:
In a rematch of their WrestleMania 42 Night 1 main event, Randy Orton defeated Cody Rhodes at WWE Sunday Night's Main Event.

While Rhodes and Orton were longtime friends dating back to their time together in the Legacy stable in the late 2000s, the dynamic changed significantly leading up to WrestleMania 42.

Orton won an Elimination Chamber match to become No. 1 contender for the WWE Championship, and Rhodes beat Drew McIntyre for the title less than a week later.

What initially seemed like it was going to be a friendly rivalry turned into something far more contentious when Orton viciously attacked Rhodes.

At WrestleMania, Rhodes took advantage of a disagreement between Orton and Pat McAfee to pin Orton and win the match, but The Viper got the last laugh by punting Cody.

Orton was not seen for months after WrestleMania, but he resurfaced at SummerSlam last month during the WWE Championship bout between Rhodes and CM Punk.

While the referee was incapacitated, Orton showed up and hit Rhodes with an RKO. Punk then executed his signature GTS to beat Cody and retain the WWE title.

In the weeks that followed SummerSlam, Rhodes and Orton were at each other's throats, leading to a grudge match between them being made official for Sunday Night's Main Event.

With both Rhodes and Orton wanting to get back in the WWE Championship mix, Sunday's bout was a huge one in terms of determining who would take a big step toward that goal.

Orton scored a major victory over The American Nightmare, which suggests a title match with Punk could be in his future.

articles.title: Satwik-Chirag breach Great Wall, China Masters win boosts Asian Games hopes
articles.summary: Badminton News: As Chirag Shetty’s winning shot landed in the middle of the court, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy let himself go — breaking into his trademark single-leg dan.
articles.body: As Chirag Shetty’s winning shot landed in the middle of the court, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy let himself go — breaking into his trademark single-leg dance, arms swinging and a broad smile lighting up his face. A delighted Chirag flung his T-shirt into the stands.Sunday, it turned out, needed to see them fall behind before it could watch them fly. The Indian duo fought back to beat China’s He Ji Ting and Ren Xiang Yu 11-21, 21-13, 21-17 in a pulsating final in Shenzhen.For a pair that has spent most of the last four years battling injuries as much as they did opponents, the title was more than just another trophy. It was a statement — and perhaps a timely reminder that the old Satwik-Chirag swagger is returning.‘We’ll go all guns blazing’Satwik Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty on Sunday became the first Indian shuttlers to win the China Masters BWF Super 750 title, and the timing could hardly have been better. With the Asian Games title defence looming later this month, the China Masters crown gives the pair exactly what they needed: belief, momentum and proof that the long road back from injury is beginning to lead somewhere familiar.“Obviously, going into the Asian Games, winning a title definitely gives a huge boost. We’ll go back home, push our- selves to the limit, train for the next 10 days and go all guns blazing at the Asian Games. We want to go out there and have some fun,” Chirag said later.Playing their third final at this tour- nament, the Indians were far from their best at the start. They were outplayed in the opening game, unable to match the pace and aggression of the Chinese pair. But just as they have done so often in their partnership, they found a way back. Even in the decider, they were staring at trou- ble at 3-7. But then came the shift.The Indians began slowing the rallies down, keeping the shuttle below the tape and refusing to allow the Chinese to un- leash their explosive attacking game. Chirag moved closer to the net, taking control of the forecourt, while Satwik found greater rhythm from the back. The comeback was on. From 16-17, the Indians produced a five-point burst that changed the complexion of the final and left the home pair with no answer.It was a finish that had been written into their script long before Sunday.“Playing here is always good. We have al- ways played here coming back from inju- ry,” a breathless Satwik later said.“I think in 2024, after the Olympics, we played here and reached the semifinals. Then last year, we played the final, though we weren’t in very good shape. I think this is also, after coming back from injury, a tournament that has given us a lot of con- fidence,” he explained.It was also a victory that vindicated the faith of their coach Kim Tan Her, who had felt Satwik was beginning to redis- cover his best after his latest injury layoff.The first game, however, gave little in- dication of what was to follow. The Indi- ans lost 11-21, struggling to impose them- selves and repeatedly allowing the Chi- nese to dictate the pace.Kim knew something had to change.“I told them to control the net and asked Chirag to stay up front and take control of the rallies. The Chinese are playing real- ly well, so we needed to counter that by locking one player at the front. It’s a great victory for them, especially with the Asian Games coming,” Kim told TOI.The message was simple: take away the Chinese attack before it gathers mo- mentum. Chirag admitted they had played into the hands of their opponents in the opening game. “I think we were not playing the right strokes. We were play- ing a style which favoured them. And when we play a style which favours them, they come all guns blazing,” he said.The China Masters, which had twice seen the Indians leave without the title — semifinalists in 2024 and runners-up last year — had finally been conquered.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
