articles.title: “I was just struggling”: George Russell admits it was tough to lose the Monza win after leading for much of the race before Kimi Antonelli passed him
articles.summary: International Sports News: George Russell left the Italian Grand Prix with a result that was hard to fully enjoy. The Mercedes driver had controlled much of the race at Monza an.
articles.body: George Russell left the Italian Grand Prix with a result that was hard to fully enjoy. The Mercedes driver had controlled much of the race at Monza and looked to be on course for victory. But a late charge from teammate Kimi Antonelli changed everything, leaving Russell with second place after a race that came down to strategy, tire life and a tense fight between the two Mercedes cars.George Russell began struggling with his tires just as Kimi Antonelli found the pace to fight him for the victoryRussell had a strong start to the race and soon moved ahead of pole sitter Pierre Gasly. From there, he looked comfortable at the front while Antonelli faced a much bigger challenge.The Italian had started from 19th on the grid. Despite that difficult position, Antonelli made rapid progress through the field and soon found himself fighting near the front.The situation became even more interesting when a Virtual Safety Car was introduced after Lance Stroll's Aston Martin stopped on track.Mercedes then split its strategy.Antonelli was brought into the pits for fresh tires, while Russell remained on the circuit. The decision initially sent Antonelli backward, but the fresher tires gave him an important advantage for the closing stages.Russell said he had expected a different approach from Mercedes.“To be honest I thought we were both going to stay out. I was surprised to see him pit,” he said.As the race moved toward its final laps, Russell began to struggle with his tires. He had stayed out on the same hard tire, leaving him with less grip as Antonelli closed the gap.“I was just struggling with the tyres towards the end,” Russell explained.Antonelli eventually got close enough to make his move. With only a few laps left, he passed Russell and took control of the race.The Italian then held on to win at his home circuit, while Russell finished second.For Russell, it was a frustrating way to lose a race he had led for so long. Still, he recognized how quickly the balance had shifted.George Russell accepted Mercedes' strategy gamble despite missing out on P1Russell could have easily focused on the disappointment of losing the victory. Instead, he gave credit to Mercedes for taking a calculated risk.The split strategy meant one driver would benefit if the fresh tires proved decisive, while the other had track position. There was no guarantee which approach would work better.“I think at the end it was a roll of the dice both ways,” Russell said.He also explained that the team could not have known for certain which choice would produce the better result.“In the moment, the team wouldn't have known which strategy was better. It made sense to split the cars but, in the end, Kimi had great pace, and there we are.”That final point was important. Antonelli did not simply benefit from the strategy. He still had to use the opportunity, and his pace allowed him to catch and pass Russell before the checkered flag.Russell was quick to praise his teammate.“Huge congratulations to Kimi of course, an incredible result from him,” he said.The victory was especially significant for Antonelli because it came at his home race after starting from the back of the field.Russell, meanwhile, was left with the feeling that second place was still a step in the right direction after a difficult period.“I'll take it, it's been more positive than it was pre-summer break and that's what I needed to try and achieve,” he said.There was still no hiding what he wanted most.“Of course I would have loved to be P1 today.”The result extended Antonelli's Drivers' Championship lead to 66 points, while Russell strengthened his position in second ahead of Lewis Hamilton.Monza therefore delivered two very different outcomes for Mercedes. Antonelli celebrated a dream home victory, while Russell had to accept that his teammate and a different tire strategy had turned a likely win into another podium.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Wrigley Field volleyball match between Nebraska and Missouri postponed after humidity leads to wild towel effort
articles.summary: Players from both teams joined event staff in trying to wipe off the court in the Wrigley Field outfield. It was just too humid to make much of a difference.
articles.body:
Nebraska and Missouri tried to play a volleyball match at Wrigley Field on Sunday night in what seemed like a fun, unique battle for the two programs as part of the Big Ten-SEC Volleyball Challenge.

It was just way, way too hot and humid in Chicago for the game to work.

The Big Ten suspended the match after a long delay on Sunday night, ending the contest early in front of a sold-out crowd at Wrigley Field. It's unclear when the match will be played between the two schools, if at all.

"Due to weather conditions affecting the court surface, Sunday's volleyball match between Nebraska and Missouri has been suspended," the Big Ten said in a statement. "Despite best efforts and in collaboration with all parties, rescheduling at Wrigley Field is not possible. A decision on match continuation at the point of suspension will be announced at a later date."

The court, which was built in the outfield of the Chicago Cubs' iconic ballpark, was incredibly slippery throughout the match. Just three points into the opening set, everybody stopped, grabbed a towel and started wiping the floor, players included.

They even started pulling up the floor decals, trying everything to make the court less slippery so it could be played on. It was quite the scene.

That seemed to do the trick, and play quickly resumed after that. At least, it did briefly.

Towels were being brought out constantly as humidity levels in Chicago were pushing 80%. Play stopped again when Nebraska jumped up 11-7 in the first set for another floor cleaning, though it was far less eventful as the first one was. Instead of cleaning the court, players from both teams started doing the "Cupid Shuffle" together. The vibes, even though volleyball wasn't being played, were incredibly high.

Eventually, after a long delay, officials opted to simply postpone the match for the night. There was a contingency plan that included playing on Monday night if needed due to weather, but the teams won't return on Monday. It's unclear if they will get to resume the match at any point this season.

No. 1 Nebraska's match with Missouri came after No. 3 Kentucky beat No. 13 Penn State in the first game of the doubleheader, which marked the first volleyball matches ever held at Wrigley Field. The first contest went off without a hitch.

While it was a great idea, and players seemed to have fun across the board despite all of the delays, volleyball at Wrigley Field just didn't work out on Sunday night.

articles.title: Who was Bill Dundee? Wrestling legend and Jerry "The King" Lawler’s longtime friend passes away at 82
articles.summary: WWE News: Bill Dundee spent more than half a century inside wrestling rings across three continents, and somehow his final on-camera moment landed just one day .
articles.body: Bill Dundee spent more than half a century inside wrestling rings across three continents, and somehow his final on-camera moment landed just one day before his death. That kind of timing doesn't happen by design, but it's exactly how Memphis wrestling said goodbye to one of its own.Dundee died early Sunday morning at 82. His son, Jamie Dundee, broke the news, and within hours tributes started pouring in from a wrestling world that had watched Dundee build his legacy over five decades.Who was Bill Dundee?Bill Dundee was born William Cruickshanks in Scotland and grew up in Australia, where his path into wrestling started in an unlikely place. As a teenager, he joined a circus and worked as a trapeze artist before ever stepping into a ring. He began wrestling professionally in Australia in the late 1960s and arrived in the United States in 1974.Memphis became his home base, and his career there became inseparable from Jerry "The King" Lawler. The two spent years shifting between fierce rivals and championship-winning partners, and their matches, built around elaborate stipulations and personal feuds, turned into some of the most memorable moments in Memphis wrestling history. Dundee also worked behind the scenes as a booker in several territories, a role that shaped the business as much as his in-ring work did.Bill Dundee dies at 82, family and WWE reactJamie Dundee announced his father's death on Facebook early Sunday, saying he died at around 3:30 a.m. and signing off, "Bill's Boy." No cause of death has been made public. Jamie had previously revealed that his father was living with stage three dementia, though nothing has tied that diagnosis to his death.WWE released a statement Sunday afternoon, writing that it was "saddened to learn that Memphis wrestling legend Bill Dundee has passed away," and extended condolences to his family and fans.Just a day earlier, Memphis Wrestling aired what turned out to be Dundee's final televised appearance, recorded before it aired Saturday on WMC. Current roster members lined up to shake his hand as announcer Dustin Starr recalled his championship battles with Lawler. Nobody watching knew it would double as a farewell.Bill Dundee's wrestling legacyDundee held the AWA Southern Heavyweight Championship nine times and the CWA International Heavyweight Championship four times, and alongside Lawler, he won the AWA World Tag Team Championship twice, including a run that began in October 1987. Their most famous feud, in 1977, carried hair stipulations and even Lawler's Cadillac as a wager.He was inducted into the Memphis Wrestling Hall of Fame in 2017, sharing the stage with Lawler, Jimmy Hart, and Koko B. Ware. Dundee kept wrestling well past his prime years, taking his final match in December 2019, nearly 45 years after he first landed in Memphis. He also spent time in WCW under the name Sir William, managing Steven Regal.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Huskies Open Season with Apple Cup Win Over Cougars
articles.summary: The 118th edition of the Apple Cup brought Washington and Washington State together for the earliest meeting in the rivalry’s history.
articles.body:
SEATTLE — The 118th edition of the Apple Cup brought Washington and Washington State together for the earliest meeting in the rivalry's history.

Normally played around Thanksgiving, this year's game was moved to the opening week of the season as college sports continue to navigate a changing landscape.

"It's the state's biggest rivalry," one fan said.

On the field, both teams took time to get going as they worked through what appeared to be early-season rust.

Washington scored its first touchdown of the season on a scramble by quarterback Demond Williams. The play was reviewed before the touchdown was confirmed, delaying the celebration for home fans.

The Huskies had been favored to win by three touchdowns; however, the game remained tight for much of the afternoon, with Washington fans waiting until late in the fourth quarter to fully celebrate the victory.

Penalties contributed to what was at times a rough contest, but UW found reasons to cheer as the game unfolded. The Huskies produced bigger plays throughout the afternoon while holding Washington State in check for much of the day.

The matchup also offered a different look than many Apple Cups in recent memory. Instead of the cold and often wet conditions associated with late-November rivalry games, fans were treated to sunny September weather.

Washington State supporters also traveled well for the game.

"This is the earliest Apple Cup ever, but we are still here; we are all over the state," one Cougars fan told KIRO 7.

The setting helped create a unique atmosphere at Husky Stadium, often considered one of college football's premier venues.

For Washington fans, the day also marked the return of quarterback Demond Williams following a tumultuous offseason. Williams delivered a strong performance, throwing for a touchdown and running for another while helping keep the Cougars at bay throughout the game.

The win gives UW a successful start to the season. The Huskies return home next Saturday to host Utah State.

Washington State will look for its first win of the season next Saturday when the Cougars travel to face Kansas State.

articles.title: Aaron Boone Drops Blunt Quote on Jasson Dominguez After Yankees Loss
articles.summary: The New York Yankees fell 4-3 to the San Diego Padres on Sunday afternoon, dropping two of three games in the series.San Diego scored three of its four runs...
articles.body:
The New York Yankees fell 4-3 to the San Diego Padres on Sunday afternoon, dropping two of three games in the series.

San Diego scored three of its four runs in the first inning, with the first three batters all hitting solo home runs off right-hander Gerrit Cole.

New York made a late push, but it ultimately wasn't enough. One of the biggest postgame storylines centered on outfielder Jasson Dominguez, who the Yankees recently recalled from Triple-A.

Dominguez made a brutal error in the second inning while starting in right field. On a routine single hit directly toward him, he failed to make the play, allowing the ball to roll to the wall and turning the single into a triple.

The Yankees escaped the inning without allowing a run, but Dominguez's struggles in the outfield remained a major talking point after the game.

Aaron Boone Drops Blunt Quote on Dominguez

During his postgame interview, Yankees manager Aaron Boone gave a blunt response when asked about Dominguez's second-inning error.

"He missed it," Boone said after a long pause . "That's what happened. Obviously, a play you gotta make. Didn't make it."

Dominguez made his Yankees debut in 2023, and while he's had some strong moments, he hasn't consistently lived up to the expectations that came with his prospect status.

His struggles in the outfield have certainly contributed to those concerns, especially after Sunday's costly error.

As for New York, the Yankees are 81-62 overall and will have Monday off before beginning a series against the Colorado Rockies on Tuesday.

They trail the Tampa Bay Rays by four games for first place in both the AL East and the American League. If the season ended today, the Yankees would hold the top Wild Card spot.

articles.summary: Lucas Carneiro kicked a 48-yard field goal as time expired to give ninth-ranked Mississippi a 41-38 victory over No. 24 Louisville on Sunday night in the Mus...
articles.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. (AP) — Lucas Carneiro kicked a 48-yard field goal as time expired to give ninth-ranked Mississippi a 41-38 victory over No. 24 Louisville on Sunday night in the Music City Kickoff .

The week's only game between ranked teams started sloppy only to turn into a second-half thriller.

Lincoln Kienholz, in his first career start after three seasons on Ohio State's bench, tied it for Louisville at 38 with 1:28 left. The quarterback found Lawayne McCoy on the sideline for a 54-yard catch-and-run TD with 4:42 to go before his 7-yard TD run with 1:28 left.

Trinidad Chambliss set up the winning field goal with an 18-yard pass on third-and-6. Chambliss finished with 351 yards passing with three touchdowns, and he also ran for a fourth score all after halftime. Kewan Lacy ran for 61 yards on 17 carries with a 1-yard TD before being sidelined by an injured thigh.

Maybe it was a bit of opening night nerves or starting with a ranked, Power Four opponent. Both Ole Miss, who ended last season losing to Miami in the College Football Playoff semifinals, and Louisville had issues in the first half.

A shotgun snap went over Chambliss' head on the opening series, and Louisville's long snapper sent the ball flying over punter Niall Hayes' head to set up a 1-yard TD run by Kewan Lacy. The Ole Miss running back ran for 61 yards on 17 carries before being sidelined by an injured thigh.

GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — CJ Carr threw two touchdown passes, Aneyas Williams ran for 90 yards and two more scores and No. 4 Notre Dame pulled away in the second half to beat Wisconsin 41-13 on Sunday night at Lambeau Field

This was the first college football game at the home of the NFL's Green Bay Packers since 2016, when Wisconsin upset a fifth-ranked LSU team 16-14. Wisconsin also hung around for a while in this one as a three-touchdown underdog before Notre Dame outscored the Badgers 28-3 in the second half.

Notre Dame's first touchdown came on a 3-yard reception by Green Bay resident James Flanigan, whose father and grandfather (each named Jim Flanigan) both played for the Packers.

Carr went 19 of 29 for 239 yards. His other touchdown completion was a 28-yarder to Nolan James Jr. with 1:51 left.

The Fighting Irish entered this season pledging to leave no doubt about their College Football Playoff worthiness after getting left out of the field last year despite winning their last 10 regular-season games by double-digit margins.

But the Irish's performance early on created plenty of doubt about how effectively they can run the ball without Heisman Trophy finalist Jeremiyah Love and Jadarian Price, the only two running backs selected in the first round of this year's NFL draft.

SEATTLE (AP) — Demond Williams Jr. threw for 268 yards and a touchdown, and Washington survived offensive struggles for a victory over Washington State in a season-opening Apple Cup.

Williams also scored on a 5-yard keeper in the 118th meeting of the two teams, who were once both part of the Pac-12. Washington won last year's meeting 59-24 in Pullman.

Transfer Caden Pinnick made his debut as quarterback for the Cougars, throwing for 142 yards and scoring on an 11-yard keeper in the fourth quarter.

Washington State was one of the remaining members of the Pac-12 left after realignment broke apart the conference ahead of the 2024 season. The Cougars and Oregon State helped re-build the conference, which now includes Boise State, Colorado State, Fresno State, San Diego State, Texas State and Utah State, along with non-football member Gonzaga.

The Huskies, meanwhile, bolted the Pac-12 for the Big Ten. Washington went 9-4 last season with a 38-10 win over Boise State in the LA Bowl.

Washington State was embarking on it's first season under coach Kirby Moore after going 7-6 last season. He brought in Pinnick, who played at UC Davis last season and threw for 3,206 yards and 32 touchdowns as a freshman.

Washington State's defense was largely effective in thwarting the Huskies throughout the game, but the Cougars missed a pair of field goals that could have narrowed the gap.

articles.title: Max Strus reveals why being a shooter is not enough to maintain a role in the NBA
articles.summary: Max Strus dives into what it's like to fight for a role in the modern NBA.
articles.body:
Standing out in the NBA as a role player can be quite challenging. They have to shine within their role and prove that they can actually contribute when their name is called by the head coach. A lot goes into the work behind the scenes because that is how they get noticed by the coaching staff.

As a career role player, Max Strus has been reliable throughout his career. He has gone from being a seldom-used player at the end of the bench to becoming a regular starter with the Cleveland Cavaliers . Now, he is playing for the Los Angeles Clippers , where he will once again be a reliable player.

Max Strus speaks on what it's like to stand out as a role player in the NBA

Standing out as a role player can be tough because there are plenty of names around the NBA who want to do the same thing. For a long time, Strus was toiling away on the bench, but when he joined the Miami Heat , he proved that he belonged on an NBA roster.

Heat head coach Erik Spoelstra saw that Strus fits into his system well because of his three-point shooting. Throughout his career, Strus is a 37% three-point shooter, which is above the average of 35%. By shooting at that clip, Strus carved out a role for himself, but that was not the only thing he did.

Throughout his career, Strus has also made a name for himself for being one of the hardest-working players. Every time he is on the court, he is defending at a high level, and he is working hard to chase the ball every time there is a loose ball. That kind of hard work and dedication to the team resonates with a lot of coaches and front office members.

"I don't have a bag. I used to have a bag back in college, but I don't anymore because you find what your niche is and you just go at it. I knew shooting the basketball was going to get me on the floor, and then I knew playing defense was going to keep me on the floor. I'll guard the best player. I don't care," Strus said about his role on the Link with JB podcast .

"You've got to have the humbleness to humble yourself to, 'I'm not that guy anymore. I can't be that guy anymore.' But then be ready for the opportunity when it does come, 'No, I could still be that guy. That's just not what we need right now. But when we do, I got you.'"

Humility goes a long way in the NBA because not everyone can be a star player. This is a reality check for a lot of NBA players, and when they realize that they can't be the star all the time, they have to shine in other ways, which is what Strus and many other standout role players have done over the years.

articles.title: Tanner ﻿Sagouspe caps rookie campaign as Fresno Grizzlies wrap 2026 regular season
articles.summary: The Fresno Grizzlies entered Sunday needing some help to prolong their 2026 season, searching for a win against the San Jose Giants and a loss from the Stock...
articles.body:
The Fresno Grizzlies entered Sunday needing help to prolong their 2026 season, seeking a win against the San Jose Giants and a loss to the Stockton Ports to secure their playoff spot.

However, neither result materialized, as the Grizzlies dropped the regular-season finale, 5-3, to the Giants on Sunday.

The bright spot came from San Joaquin Memorial alum Tanner Sagouspe, whom the Colorado Rockies drafted in the ninth round of the 2026 MLB Draft after playing his collegiate ball at Cal Poly and TCU.

Sagouspe came on in relief, shoving two innings while allowing no hits or runs and striking out three, with his family in attendance.

With the loss on Sunday, the season comes to an end for the Grizzlies, but Sagouspe said he's fortunate to get the opportunity to show out for his hometown team.

"Being able to play in front of my community and family, most importantly, has been awesome," Sagouspe said. "Couldn't have written it up any better than to be able to come back home and play for Fresno."

The Grizzlies end the season with a 69-63 overall record.

articles.title: Reds Overcome Brady Singer’s Worst Start of Season to Beat Brewers
articles.summary: Elly De La Cruz and Tyler Stephenson ignited a massive offensive rally to rescue a shaky rotation, clinching a rare series victory despite a career-high walk...
articles.body:
Cincinnati Reds have won their first series against the Milwaukee Brewers in a long time, powered by offensive explosions from Elly De La Cruz and Tyler Stephenson to do so. De La Cruz had two hits and four runs batted in, including an opposite-field home run from the right side. Stephenson had two hits and two runs batted in.

They weren't helped, however, by starting pitcher Brady Singer . The right-hander allowed six earned runs and walked six for what was statistically the worst start of the season for Singer. It was both the most walks and earned runs Singer had allowed in a game this season and the most earned runs he's allowed since July 21, 2025. He set a career high for walks allowed.

Singer had a quiet first three innings, allowing just two baserunners after being given a three-run cushion by the Reds' offense. Brewers left-handed hitter Jake Bauers struck for a loud home run to cut the Reds' lead to just two. Singer floated an 82 mph slider in the lower part of the strike zone, but it was nonetheless in Bauers' wheelhouse for a long home run.

Garrett Mitchell then very nearly left the yard to center field in the Brewers' next at-bat, but banged it off the center field wall for a stand-up triple. Singer again had a slider catch too much of the plate.

Cooper Pratt laid down a safety squeeze bunt later in the inning, and Singer threw the ball into the backstop in a really ugly-looking play, leading to Milwaukee putting runners at second and third after the run scored. Singer then retired back-to-back hitters to limit the damage and get out of the jam.

Singer picked up two quick outs in the fifth inning, but then walked two straight, bringing up Garrett Mitchell again. He hit a line drive into left-center field to score a run and make it a two-run game after Elly De La Cruz's two-run home run in the previous inning. At 94 pitches, Terry Francona decided to keep Singer in the game. On his next pitch, Brewers middle infielder Brice Turang lined one down the right-field line to score two runs and tie the game.

He got out of the fifth inning, and the Reds retook the lead on a two-run double by Elly De La Cruz in the next half-inning, leading to the incredibly rare feat of a pitcher giving up six earned runs and being credited with the win.

articles.body:
It's game week! The Cincinnati Bengals play the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Paycor Stadium to open the 2026 season. Tampa Bay's win total over/under is currently 8.5 as they have navigated an offseason with contract drama surrounding quarterback Baker Mayfield and defensive tackle Vita Vea.

Here are some of the biggest storylines surrounding Sunday's game in Cincinnati.

The defensive end injured his left knee in the first training camp. After the gruesome video and Stewart being carted off, it appeared it would be a long-term injury. The Bengals got lucky: it turned out to be a hyperextension, and Stewart immediately had a chance to play in Week 1, despite the fact the Bengals had no timetable for a return.

He recently returned to practice after a month-long absence and took part in position drills with his fellow defensive linemen. I don't really think the Bengals need to rush Stewart back, which is a testament to their depth on the defensive line, but there are a lot of people who think Stewart could make a big second-year jump after a disappointing rookie season.

Does the under-center/play-action uptick lead to explosiveness?

The Bengals made a concerted effort to increase under-center snaps and play action during training camp. Cincinnati has struggled with explosive plays over the past few seasons. As they tried to ease into this new offensive scheme, they struggled, and Cincinnati's defense no doubt won most of the early practices.

This will be a sticking point for fans, especially if they struggle early. While Cincinnati hasn't been too explosive, they have been efficient and put up a lot of points over the past few seasons. However, few doubt Joe Burrow can handle this shift in offensive approach.

Does Cincinnati get immediate returns from Dexter Lawrence?

Lawrence wreaked havoc in training camp, making plays and doing things that very few football players on earth can do. The interception against the Chicago Bears in joint camp, grabbing and stopping Chase Brown with one arm. The expectations coming into the season were high, but after his stellar training camp, they are even higher.

He is going to draw a double team on most snaps, and whether or not he's able to make game-changing plays will be something people are watching for. If Lawrence posts a big fourth-quarter sack followed by an offensive score, it could tangibly show the difference between last year's defense and this season's.

articles.body: PUNE: Elavenil Valarivan is just 27, but she is already one of the ‘oldest’ shooters in India’s team for the Asian Games.With two Olympics, more than a dozen of World Cups, World Championships and Asian Championships and nine years of shooting under her name, she is certainly the richest in terms of experience. And yet, the Ahmedabad shooter will be excited as a fresher when she takes aim at the 10m air rifle competitions at the Asian Games in Nagoya-Aich, Japan, later this month.Elavenil, who had missed the bus for the 2023 edition of the Asian Games, is happy to be back for the continental Games. “I’m grateful to be a part of the Asian Games again. I’m very excited to participate as 2025 and 2026 have been pleasant years for me. I’ve been pretty satisfied with myself so I’m just looking forward to doing the absolute same thing and being myself,” the Tokyo and Paris Games participant told TOI during the national camp in Bhopal.Elavenil had heartbreaks in the two Olympic participations, but the shooter feels disappointment is bound to happen as so much ride on the quadrennial Games.“The Olympics are different because it’s once in four years and it is the most celebrated sporting tournament in the world. You have expectations, and no matter how much you say, ‘No, no, I don’t have any expectations’, at the end of the day, you know it is important to you, and that’s where the expectations arise,” she said.Born to Tamil parents, Elavenil grew up in Ahmedabad and started shooting when she was 13. Since then, she was tuned to win medals. But now, she just doesn’t chase medals.“At Tokyo I was a young athlete. Coping with the Tokyo disappointment was something that took all my energy. That learning helped me for Paris. After Paris, I think my perspective has changed. Till Paris, it was about winning the medal. Now, it is more about enjoying the sport, and the results are showing,” Elavenil said.The rifle shooter has also made friends off the range.“Last year my brother got married and he was busy with his life so I really wanted to have a life of my own. articles.title: Catch Yankees' Dave Winfield (and his new book) at these NJ events
articles.summary: Baseball Hall of Famer Dave Winfield is out with a new book, "Touching All the Bases: A Story of Power, Purpose, and Surviving the Bronx."
articles.body:
What isn't there to know about Dave Winfield?

After all, he was the star center fielder for the New York Yankees throughout most of the 1980s, where he played in a World Series, almost won a batting title, and famously feuded with the team's competitive and controversial owner, George Steinbrenner. That battle with "The Boss" threatened to end Winfield's career and led to Steinbrenner being banned from baseball in 1990 (repealed after two years) after the owner paid gambler Howard Spira $40,000 to find dirt on Winfield.

Winfield is a 12-time All-Star in the Baseball Hall of Fame, but could have been in the Basketball or even Football Hall of Fame, as one of only three professional athletes drafted by four sports leagues (MLB, NFL, NBA, and ABA).

But as Winfield said in a recent interview with NorthJersey.com about his new book, "Touching All the Bases: A Story of Power, Purpose, and Surviving the Bronx," co-authored with veteran journalist and NJ resident Alan Maimon (Matt Holt Books; 288 pg. $31; Sept. 15), there is so much more readers will learn than what has been reported, from his upbringing in St. Paul, Minnesota to the Steinbrenner feud to the present day.

However, he teased while speaking to NorthJersey.com reporter: "You have to read the book."

The former Fort Lee and Teaneck resident, who has authored five books, will be appearing at several locations in North Jersey to promote the book:

Sept. 11, from 5 to 7 p.m., book signing at the Yogi Berra Museum & Learning Center, 8 Yogi Berra Dr., Little Falls. Tickets are $40, including admission and the book.

Sept. 13 from 10 a.m. to noon, book signing and meet-and-greet at Books & Greetings, 271 Livingston Street, Northvale. Attendees must purchase a book or ticket to enter. For more details, call the store at (201) 784-2665. Then, at 1 p.m., he will be appearing at Bookends, 211 E Ridgewood Ave. Ridgewood. Attendees need to purchase a book for entry. For more information, visit book-ends.org .

The following is a transcript of a phone interview with Winfield, edited for space and clarity.

I led a very interesting life, and I just felt it was time to share a lot of this. People think that they know what my life and career were all about, but they really don't. There are a lot of stories, a lot of experiences. Things in sports, labor issues, and life experiences I needed to tell.

There are many stories and experiences my family has never heard, friends never heard, and guys I played with never heard.

What was the most difficult part of writing the book?

I think getting it right. Make sure I tell the truth, connect the dots, and have it in my voice. I think it was the most important part. When you work with somebody like a writer, they don't necessarily know your voice. They may know something about your experience, but they may not know something about your voice.

What was your favorite part of writing this book?

Sharing with people that I was just a kid with a dream, that I wanted to be a professional baseball player by the time I was 12 years old. Once I was in that process and I was living that dream, there were a lot of adversities, from injuries to not playing or accomplishing what I set out to do in a couple of games. I think I'm very happy at this point; people will see me for who I really am.

What was your favorite moment with the Yankees?

I think the guys I played with. There was a connection between some of the Yankees' past and history. To be able to interact with guys like Yogi Berra, who was my manager for a bit. You just sit and talk with Mickey Mantle and Joe DiMaggio.

I just enjoyed playing with a number of good players. We had some good teams. We didn't always have great pitching. Offensively, we had some good teams; we had some good guys. The fans were behind us everywhere we traveled.

Looking back as you did in this memoir, do you regret playing for the New York Yankees?

No. To have a chance to play for a historical team, a chance to win it all. The things I was looking for, I was hoping for. It was a big piece of my life. I had high ambitions for it. To be detoured, for those things I couldn't predict. I wouldn't wish it on anybody.

What is it like coming back to North Jersey to talk about the book and meet fans?

I always come back to New York and New Jersey three or four times a year. You can see it's quite a busy schedule. I have never been to the Yogi Berra Center. Looking forward to it. Seeing a lot of people.

What do you hope readers take away from reading this book?

First of all, they know me much better. They see what it took to create a legendary career from far-from-normal circumstances. I think most people will enjoy it. I was glad to download these stories and experiences and share them with people.

articles.title: ETSU looks to sharpen execution after first win of the season over Tusculum
articles.summary: JOHNSON CITY, Tenn. (WJHL) — ETSU football got back in the win column Saturday, but head coach Will Healy knows there is still plenty to clean up as the Bucc...
articles.body:
JOHNSON CITY, Tenn. (WJHL) — ETSU football got back in the win column Saturday, but head coach Will Healy knows there is still plenty to clean up as the Buccaneers prepare for their first road test of the season.

The Bucs evened their record at 1-1 with a 48-14 win over Tusculum, finishing with 259 passing yards and 225 yards on the ground. Freshman quarterback Mason Mims completed 13 of 21 passes, while running back TJ Peyton rushed for a career-high 121 yards and two touchdowns on 11 carries.

Despite the lopsided victory, Healy said lapses in execution remain a concern.

"We have explosive ability in all three phases, but we are not near consistent enough," Healy said. "We have mental lapses that are going to get us beat, lapses that got us beat a week ago."

That Week 1 loss to Campbell left a "bitter taste" for the Bucs, according to linebacker Jarvis Johnson. ETSU responded by putting an emphasis on discipline and preparation against Tusculum.

"When you're going against a team like that, you just got to be very disciplined. This week we had keys. You got to keep your eye on your key. If not, they're going to go for a big run," Johnson said. "When we play teams like Citadel and VMI, we just got to do the same thing with the preparation we did this week, a lot of scout periods and just staying tuned in with your key."

The Bucs will now look to carry that preparation into a much tougher test. ETSU hits the road for the first time this season next week, traveling to Chapel Hill to take on North Carolina.

articles.title: Louisville comes up just short against No. 9 Ole Miss
articles.summary: Too many self-inflicted mistakes and a sensational second half from arguably the best quarterback in college football were the stories as Louisville opened i...
articles.body:
Too many self-inflicted mistakes and a sensational second half from arguably the best quarterback in college football were the stories as Louisville opened its 2026 season with a last-second, 41-38 loss to No. 9 Ole Miss Sunday night in Nashville.

New U of L quarterback Lincoln Kienholz rallied the Cards from a 38-24 fourth quarter deficit, tossing a 54-yard touchdown to Lawayne McCoy and then running another in a series later to even the score. Unfortunately, the 1:41 on the clock was too much time for Trinidad Chambliss, perhaps the best quarterback in college football, and Lucas Carneiro, perhaps the best kicker in college football.

After a first half that saw him both lose a fumble and toss an interception, Chambliss picked the Cardinal secondary apart in the second 30 minutes. The Heisman hopeful tossed for three touchdowns, including a pair of 62-yard bombs to Deuce Alexander, and scampered for another score to kick off his sixth and final(?) season of college ball.

Two of those Rebel touchdowns were aided dramatically by key Cardinal penalties. With eight minutes to play in the fourth quarter, U of L had appeared to take possession of the ball down just seven points when Ole Miss kicker Lucas Carneiro's 57-yard attempt came up short. However, cornerback D.J. Waller was whistled for roughing the kicker, and Chambliss carried the ball into the endzone to put the Rebels up 14 seven plays later.

The only Ole Miss touchdown of the first half was set up by a snap that sailed over U of L punter Niall Hayes' head, forcing him to fall on the football on the Cardinal 12-yard-line.

"We wanted to do something special, but we came up short," Louisville head coach Jeff Brohm said. "I'm proud of my team, but in the end we didn't do enough. The snap over the kickers head, costly. The roughing the kicker, costly."

Adding insult was the fact that this was the first time in the Jeff Brohm era where Louisville has won the turnover battle but come up short on the scoreboard. The Cards had previously been 17-0 under Brohm when committing fewer turnovers than their opponents, and 13-0 when committing zero penalties.

Ole Miss was very shaky early on in this one, and Louisville not taking advantage of that is ultimately where it feels like the Cards lost the game. You were +2 in turnovers, you limited one of the most explosive offenses in the country to just over 100 total yards … and you trailed 10-6 at the break.

Even with that being the case, it's hard to be entirely gloom and doom after this one.

I spent most of the summer saying I didn't feel great about this game, but I did feel great about this team. I'm doubling down on the second part of that equation after tonight.

The penalties and the poor game management were maddening at times, but the pieces are there. I wouldn't have been able to say that if Kienholz hadn't stepped up the way he did in the second half … but he did. That kid is a warrior, and while his early jitters were apparent to everyone watching, leading two successful must-score drives in the final minutes of a game against a team that was a play away from the title game last year is a pretty strong sign for the couple of months ahead.

There is zero time for wound licking or moral victory back-patting: The next 13 days loom extremely large for any hope of having a "special" season.

articles.title: 'We are so screwed': Fans react as Australia announces squad for South Africa Test series, Marnus Labuschagne survives selection
articles.summary: Australia have retained Marnus Labuschagne despite his poor recent form, leaving fans questioning the selectors' decision.
articles.body:
Marnus Labuschagne retains his place in Australia 's 16-man Test squad for South Africa .

Labuschagne scored 1,659 runs at 29.69, with no century since 2023.

Ricky Ponting recently urged Australian selectors to drop Labuschagne, calling his place "almost untenable."

Fans have questioned Australia's reluctance to change its top order.

Australia Test squad for South Africa: Key changes and Marnus Labuschagne selection

Australia has kept most of the team members who played in the recently drawn 1- 1 Test series against Bangladesh . The team consists of three new members with all-rounder Cooper Connolly, spinner Matthew Kuhnemann and experienced bowler Michael Neser.

The first Test takes place in Durban from October 9, with the rest of the series being held in Gqeberha and Cape Town.

With Australia drawing a 1-1 series against Bangladesh and their batting unit getting criticised again, Marnus Labuschagne's selection has become the biggest issue for Australia before their South Africa tour with him even dropping out of the ODI side during the Proteas tour.

Australia Test squad: Pat Cummins (c), Scott Boland, Alex Carey, Cooper Connolly, Cameron Green, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Josh Inglis, Matthew Kuhnemann, Marnus Labuschagne, Nathan Lyon, Michael Neser, Matthew Renshaw, Steve Smith, Mitchell Starc, Beau Webster.

Marnus Labuschagne's recent struggles continue

The case for retaining Labuschagne is inseparable from his shocking failure in Tests post-2022, culminating in his barely making 36 runs during the Bangladesh Test series.

At the 2025-26 Ashes, he aggregated 259 runs across 10 innings at 28.77.

After being one of the best Test batters in the world, he has managed only 1,659 runs at an average of 29.69 since the beginning of 2023.

In fact, his average has deteriorated from 34.91 in 2023 to 30.93 in 2024 and a measly 20.84 in 2025, and he has not touched double digits in the Tests since the fourth Ashes Test in July 2023.

His latest performance against Bangladesh saw Labuschagne score 1 and 31 in the first Test, while he was dismissed for 4 in the next match, accumulating just 36 runs in three innings.

Ricky Ponting wanted Australia to drop Labuschagne

Ricky Ponting called for Australia to forget Marnus Labuschagne due to his recent lackluster form. Labuschagne scored a mere 36 runs in the three innings he played against Bangladesh, prompting Ponting to say that his inclusion in the Test side is "almost untenable." He further recommended that Australia should find itself a new No. 3 batter.

Further, Ponting advocated that Australia play Travis Head in the middle order and include another younger batter in the top order. He also pointed out that Australia should consider changing their batting lineup before their upcoming tough Test series in South Africa.

Fans furious after Marnus Labuschagne survives

One of the most direct barrages read, "Absolute idiots - we are so screwed in the near future. George Bailey is such a dud."

Another follower criticised the continued trust placed in the same batting lineup in Australia, asking, "When are we gonna change ? No point keep picking the same top 6 that fails time and time again. Especially our number 3."

Labuschagne's selection was also commented upon negatively, with one fan describing the decision as a "reward" and questioning if the selectors themselves were pushing the fans away from the sport.

Yet another remark concerned the selectors' unwillingness to select young players: "My God, they hate to give the kids a go don't they?"

While questions over Labuschagne's selection continued, a summary of the apparent superficiality of the incumbent No. 3 batsman was given by one fan, stating that there was "No real option at 3 if (when) Labuschagne fails again".

Retaining Labuschagne could prove a costly gamble for Australia

There is definitely an argument that Labuschagne should not be dropped. He is still an experienced Test player with 65 Tests and 11 hundreds and conditions in South Africa can suit an experienced player.

However, it is not a temporary fall of form that Labuschagne has. His average has fallen each year from 2023 to 2025; he hasn't scored a hundred in more than three years, and in his last Test series, he scored only 36 runs.

While Ponting's views make us see what Australia could have done if it had thought that a change was coming, for the time being, Labuschagne gets another chance. But after this vote of confidence, pressure on the Australian No. 3 batter will be enormous from the first ball in Durban.

articles.title: Christopher Bell was in rare comedic form after winning the Southern 500
articles.summary: This is the biggest win of his career and came at the perfect time in the season
articles.body:
Christopher Bell was downright effusive after winning the Southern 500.

There have been big victories over the years from the Chili Bowl Midget Nationals and the World of Outlaws to wins across all three national touring divisions including the Coca-Cola 600 and Bristol Night Race.

But the Southern 500 is the biggest of them all to date.

"Wow, what a night," Bell said afterwards. "Darlington is literally the track that -- it is NASCAR . Like, there is no other track that's harder to drive, that rewards a talented driver more than Darlington and the Southern 500. This is the epitome of NASCAR, and I'm just super grateful to be here.

"Yeah, it's better than a dream come true."

Christopher Bell, No. 20 Joe Gibbs Racing Toyota

To say that he was in tremendous spirits afterwards would be an understatement. As this victory was also the kickoff for the Chase for the Championship, and not the previous Cup Series Playoffs format, he had jokes about his excitement for that too.

"I was debating on coming in here and making a joke about my two off weeks that I get since I won, I advance to the next round, I get to take the next two weeks off, but it ain't happening this year," Bell said with a downright giddy grin on his face. "And I love it. I absolutely love it. That's the way it's supposed to be.

"Yeah, we're off to a great start, but no off weeks. Right back to work next week at Gateway and going have to -- I still believe that I will have to win more races in the Chase if I want to be the champion.

"Yeah, so we're off to a really good start, but there's no more off weeks, and I love it."

Again, this is a guy that has a rain-shorted Coca-Cola 600 and Bristol Night Race win, but this is the pinnacle for him and his entire No. 20 Joe Gibbs Racing team. This one just means more.

"Yeah, I always have because this racetrack is so hard, and the 500 miles here is just -- it is the ultimate test of mental toughness and just keeping yourself in it," Bell said. "My Coke 600 is amazing, but I wish it was 600 miles, so hopefully -- yeah, hopefully I get another opportunity at the Coke 600.

"Yeah, I mean, obviously the Daytona 500, the Brickyard are races that everybody wants to win, but you know, these are the driver ones for sure."

Bell, the driver, had to work for this one too.

He had just won the second stage when a slow pit stop dropped them to outside of the top 10 for the ensuing restart. In real time, crew chief Adam Stevens was unfazed.

"We don't know what the fuckin' future holds," he told Bell over the radio. "We're going to make the best out of the situation we have. We don't know when that downstream caution is going to fall, and that's what is going to decide this race."

There were indeed cautions, including one where the pit crew made up for their earlier error, giving them the lead off pit road. Then came the caution where the pit but Kyle Larson stayed out. Bell briefly lost a spot to Chase Elliott but drove back around and eventually picked off Larson, who was on a tire deficit.

There were several moments where Bell thought he was going to add to his seven runner-up finishes since his last win 33 races ago. He thought he was going to remain winless this season.

That's why he was so excited afterwards.

"It was probably that damn winless streak I was on," Bell said. "It makes me probably appreciate this more and soak it in more. You never know when your next win is going to come, if this is your last one.

"Yeah, that was too long. That was too long to go without winning, especially with the product that we're racing with, the Toyota race cars. I mean, they're absolutely incredible. Everyone else is winning … And we've been so close. We've been in position. I knew it was just a matter of time, but it was frustrating to go that long without winning."

Bell also has reason to be excited about his championship pursuit too. He entered this race as the No. 6 seed, 50 points behind Denny Hamlin, and leaves Darlington just a dozen points back.

"I believe that the champion is going to be a Toyota," Bell said. "I said that all week at media day. Then we've got four great drivers (and) great teams. I don't know. I mean, I go back to 2019 when all four of the JGR cars were incredible. This is right there with it.

"All of us are still in contention for the title. I believe it will be one of us four or, you know, one of the 23XI cars. We just have a great product right now, and TRD, Toyota has given us that platform, and our teams have hit it. Yeah, we need to make the most of it now, because we know how it goes. Right now we're on top, but we won't be up there forever, that's for sure."

Before the press conference ended, Bell left with one more joke too -- one about a shared theme between himself and O'Reilly Series race winner Sheldon Creed.

They have both been defined by second-place finishes.

"This is very ironic," Bell said. "We saved the best question for last, guys! Sheldon Creed won and Christopher Creed won. How about that? Oh, my gosh. … This is hilarious. That is absolutely hilarious. But, yeah, good stuff."

articles.title: Kyle Shanahan praises 49ers fans, takes shot at Rams on Australia game
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan isn't happy about playing the Los Angeles Rams in Australia for one key reason.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan hasn't exuded excitement about his team having to open its season with an international game. Part of that had to do with 49ers fans.

Shanahan on Sunday while speaking with reporters in Australia said part of the reason he had misgivings about the Week 1 matchup was that despite the Los Angeles Rams being the designated home team, he feels like it's the 49ers giving up a home game.

"It's cool for us, just we always have an advantage of having one, I see it as one home game a year in L.A.," Shanahan said. "Just the way our fans are and take over that stadium. So, it was disappointing to let them off the hook and get them out of that. But, I have a feeling knowing how our fans roll, I have a feeling they won't be much different here. I expect to have a good showing. I wouldn't say it hit me right on the plane, but after being here for a couple days, this is the right time to be here, it's the right place to be and it's the right team to go against."

49ers fans have typically taken over SoFi Stadium to the point the Rams offense has had to go to a silent count at home. Since Shanahan took over as the 49ers coach in 2017 his club is 7-2 in nine regular season games vs. the Rams at SoFi Stadium, including a wild 26-23 overtime win last year without Brock Purdy, George Kittle, Nick Bosa and Ricky Pearsall.

Shanahan multiple times in his press conference expressed the importance of every game across an 18-week season, which led to some of his displeasure with the potential competitive impact on having the game on another continent.

However, it wouldn't be a surprise to a see a sea of red at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on Thursday evening. 49ers fans not only travel, but they're popular internationally as well, so Shanahan's concerns about losing the road home game may not be a problem.

articles.title: College volleyball debut at Wrigley Field suspended for slick court
articles.summary: CHICAGO — The second volleyball match Sunday night at Wrigley Field in the SEC-Big Ten Challenge was suspended because of excessive moisture on the court. Th...
articles.body:
CHICAGO — The second volleyball match Sunday night at Wrigley Field in the SEC-Big Ten Challenge was suspended because of excessive moisture on the court.

The decision was made to prevent injuries after players slipped several times on the wet surface.

With a sellout crowd of 43,067 energized for the first volleyball event at the iconic home of the Chicago Cubs, third-ranked Kentucky beat No. 11 Penn State in four sets in the opening match — just an appetizer for fans of the top-ranked Huskers, who filled nearly all of the seats at Wrigley.

Ideal conditions — or so it seemed — awaited Nebraska and Missouri. But the first set was stopped for more than 15 minutes after 2 points. Players from both teams dried the TeraFlex floor with towels as the humidity levels of a 72-degree night pushed past 80 percent.

"This was amazing," Nebraska coach Dani Busboom Kelly said. "I applaud the effort. But there's a reason our sport's indoors."

She said she would not favor outdoor volleyball events in the future. Famously, Nebraska initiated the momentum that led to Sunday with a match played at Memorial Stadium in August 2023 that drew a crowd of 92,003, a world record for a women's sporting event.

In a venture operated jointly by the Big Ten and the Cubs on Sunday, staff brought battery-powered blowers to the court, but moisture continued to gather as the first set progressed. Towels couldn't keep up. Action was stopped again as Nebraska led 11-7.

The teams engaged in a dance contest on the court for several minutes, keeping fans entertained as a singalong ensued in the seats. A 15-minute break was called. Both teams left the court for their locker rooms before the suspension was announced.

Nebraska's four seniors — Harper Murray, Laney Choboy, Andi Jackson and Bergen Reilly — spoke to the crowd after the announcement that the match would not continue.

"Thank you for supporting women's sports," Jackson said.

The idea for Sunday was born in January 2025 in the Wrigley suite of Crane Kenney, the Cubs president, who hosted the Big Ten commissioner to watch the Frozen Confines, a two-day hockey event that featured Big Ten men's and women's teams.

"At the Cubs, we like to take on big and crazy things," said Colin Faulkner, the Cubs' chief commercial officer. "Big and crazy ideas. That's in our DNA and our nature."

The Big Ten and SEC worked to get three former national-championship programs and Missouri, the SEC school with the largest alumni base in Chicago.

The Cubs completed a homestand Thursday. Immediately, work began to prep the surface. Construction of the playing court took most of Friday. The weather cooperated through the weekend — until it didn't.

articles.title: Kyle Larson doesn't regret strategic gamble he took at Darlington despite coming up short
articles.summary: Kyle Larson's gamble didn't result in a win, but he still held on for a solid finish at Darlington.
articles.body:
Sometimes to win in the NASCAR Cup Series, you have to take a gamble. And sometimes, that gamble simply doesn't work out.

Such was the case for Kyle Larson on Saturday, who made the decision to stay out on the track with 24 laps to go at Darlington. All but four other cars pitted to take fresh tires.

The decision put Larson in the race lead, where he would do his best to fend off those on fresher tires hunting him down. While he held on admirably, eventually he was caught and passed by Christopher Bell with 12 laps left to race.

After the race, Larson was asked if he regretted the decision to stay out. He instantly turned the offer down, standing by his team's strategy.

"No. I don't. Because we were going to restart behind the No. 20, the No. 19, it was going to be tough coming to my pit stall around the No. 54."

Larson said that while he stands by the move, he did think that he would have a little more support on the alternative strategy he was running, and didn't realize how many cars would choose to pit.

"I was actually surprised that they pitted in front of me, and I was then surprised that not more stayed out with me," Larson said. "I just thought there were so many cars on the lead lap, I thought there might be, I don't know, two to four more that might stay out. I thought that that could help me at least get some laps where I could manage my tires. But Bell got to second so fast, I was just straight into defense and not able to run the lines that I ultimately wanted to to take care of my tires."

Larson held off Bell as long as he could, and once passed by him, did his best defensive driving to hold on for as high a finish as he could manage. He wound up in fifth, which is a solid result for the first race of the Chase.

"We only gained six points to the lead, but it's better than losing six," he said.

Larson will have the chance to gain more on the Chase lead next weekend as the Cup Series heads to Illinois.

articles.title: Vikings 2026 Season Forecast
articles.summary: It’s time for my annual Vikings season forecast. And like my forecasts for the rest of the NFC North teams, I will be looking at roster/coaching changes this...
articles.body:
It's time for my annual Vikings season forecast. And like my forecasts for the rest of the NFC North teams, I will be looking at roster/coaching changes this offseason, injuries and luck factors from last season, and the change in strength of schedule from last season to this season to guide my forecast.

One thing you never find attached to any pundit's predictions is their track record, except this one. Predicting outcomes of football games and seasons is far from an exact science, but there are some key factors that can and do impact a team's season, some of which are not immediately obvious. Nevertheless, there are so many interrelated variables involved that perfection is impossible. My own track record is far from perfect, but since I started using my current formula I've at least been closer than the over/under total two of the last three seasons- 2023 being way off due to Kirk Cousins going down mid-season. In any case, this will be my tenth prediction over the past eleven seasons, having abandoned any prediction in 2016 after Teddy Bridgewater went down just prior to the start of the season. Here are the results:

2015 : Prediction: 10-6. Actual: 11-5. Preseason over/under: 7.5

2016 : No prediction after Bridgewater went down. Acutal: 8-8. Preseason over/under: 9.5 (pre-Bridgewater injury).

2017 : Prediction: 12-4. Actual: 13-3. Preseason over/under: 8.5

2018 : Prediction: 13-3. Actual: 8-7-1. Preseason over/under: 10

2019 : Prediction: 11-5. Actual: 10-6. Preseason over/under: 9.

2020 : Prediction: 11-5. Actual: 7-9. Preseason over/under: 8.5 (March)

2021 : Prediction: 13-4. Actual: 8-9. Preseason over/under: 9.

2022 : Prediction: 12-5. Actual: 13-4. Preseason over/under: 9.5.

2023 : Prediction: 11-6. Actual: 7-10. Preseason over/under: 8.5.

2024 : Prediction: 10-7. Actual: 14-3. Preseason over/under: 6.5.

2025 : Prediction: 11-6. Actual: 9-8. Preseason over/under: 9.

The most difficult aspect of predicting the Vikings season record the past few years has been the lack of continuity at the quarterback position. In 2023, Kirk Cousins went down mid-season, leading to a trio of backups – one of which wasn't on the roster at the beginning of the season- trying to manage the rest of the way. 2024 saw the reclamation of Sam Darnold, who I was optimistic about compared to most but not optimistic enough as it turned out. And last year I was too optimistic about J.J. McCarthy's ability to have a Sam Darnold-like season, based on a piece I did in April 2025 that compiled the average stats of first-round quarterbacks landing in 'good' situations in their first full season as a starter. Of the 27 quarterbacks I measured in that piece, only Mark Sanchez had a slightly worse season than McCarthy did last year in terms of passer rating and ANY/A and it's fair to say that Sanchez did not have the offensive weapons that McCarthy had (he did have the top defense). Given McCarthy's relative performance compared to his backups last season, it didn't really matter that he missed seven games and departed a couple others early due to injury.

Minnesota Vikings Last Season and Offseason Changes

The Vikings finished 9-8, including 4-2 in the division last season which resulted in a third-place finish. They managed to win nine games despite the second-worst quarterbacking in the league (above only the Browns) and the most giveaways in the league (30), based on a roughly top five defense and only two missed field goals all season. At one point the Vikings were 4-8 but took advantage of a soft remaining schedule to win their last five games.

They have continuity this season in coaching with Kevin O'Connell, Wes Phillips, Matt Daniels, and Brian Flores all returning as head coach and coordinators. Brian Flores was extended and is now believed to be the highest paid coordinator in league history.

It is noteworthy that the Vikings added Frank Smith as assistant head coach who is the de facto run game coordinator. In terms of baseline scheme, the Vikings will remain primarily an outside zone running team, but Frank Smith, who served as offensive coordinator under Mike McDaniel in Miami the past few years, along with Keith Carter as offensive line coach, will bring some innovation and greater attention to detail that the Vikings' run game has been missing. The Vikings didn't show much of their new run game in the preseason, but there has been a lot of buzz about it in training camp. We'll see if it was warranted.

The big offseason addition was quarterback Kyler Murray, who the Vikings are hoping will raise their quarterback play from the bottom of the league to at least league average, if not higher. Unlike Sam Darnold, the Vikings previous quarterback reclamation project, Murray comes to the Vikings with roughly league average, rather than considerably worse, performance metrics. Both Murray and Darnold had mediocre teams around them in their pre-Vikings careers as starters.

It's worth noting that Murray has been an above league-average quarterback over his pro career with the Cardinals, which if he was able to maintain that this season would be a major improvement over the Vikings' 2025 quarterback performance. Murray's QBR rankings ( an adjusted EPA-based metric ) each season since being drafted #1 overall in 2019:

By contrast, the Vikings QBR last season- weighted average of McCarthy (35.6), Wentz (43.3), and Brosmer (14.3)- was 35.4. The way QBR is formulated, a league-average quarterback is meant to have a 50 QBR. This metric also represents the percentage chance the quarterback's team would be expected to win, all other factors being equal, given the quarterback's performance. Over Murray's career, he has a season average QBR of 58.0.

By contrast, Sam Darnold's season average QBR prior to joining the Vikings was 42.9. Darnold had a 57.3 QBR in his season with the Vikings.

Outside of Murray's ACL injury shortened years of 2022-2023- also years the Cardinals defense ranked 31st in points allowed- and last season when he only played in five games (and had a 29th ranked defense), Murray has been an above average starting quarterback in QBR ranking and cracked the top ten in the two most recent seasons. And he did so in two significantly different schemes. When Murray has had an above average defense in points allowed (15th in 2024, 11th in 2021, 12th in 2020) his QBR has been in the low 60s. That's not an unreasonable baseline expectation this season, given the team around him and Murray's QBR history.

Offensively, outside of quarterback, the Vikings replaced WR3 Jalen Nailor with Jauan Jennings, who isn't the athletic downfield threat Nailor was but may fit better with the Vikings scheme this year as a big, tough, contested catch, move-the-chains type receiver who can also block. Blake Brandel, who started 7 games last year at center, and took snaps there in a few others, takes over as the starter this season from the retired Ryan Kelly. The Vikings also replaced the retired C.J. Ham with Max Bredeson at fullback. They also added Demond Claiborne as RB3. Overall these are minor roster changes compared to last year's roster.

Defensively, the Vikings traded edge rusher Jonathan Greenard to the Eagles, promoting Dallas Turner to the starting job and recently acquired Kyle Van Noy to provide experienced and capable depth. The Vikings also moved on from Javon Hargrave and Jonathan Allen at defensive tackle, promoting Levi Drake-Rodriquez and Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins while drafting Caleb Banks in the first round and Domonique Orange in the third round. Elijah Williams will also rotate at defensive tackle this season and looked good in preseason and joint practices. The Vikings also drafted linebacker Jake Golday in the second round.

In the defensive secondary, the Vikings will likely have the same starting lineup with the return of Harrison Smith but have added veteran James Pierre at cornerback along with promising 5th round pick Charles Demmings, and at safety added promising UDFA Jacob Thomas and third-round pick Jakobe Thomas. Overall, these defensive roster changes are not enough to warrant a change in forecasted win total this season.

But the big change is at quarterback and that warrants a significant three-game adjustment to the Vikings win total this season.

Last season the Vikings ranked 9th in adjusted games lost (AGLs) , despite losing their starting quarterback for seven games (and leaving halfway through two more). That is roughly average for teams with Tyler Williams as head of their training/sports science staffs, which prior to coming to the Vikings included the Rams as well. Here is his AGL track record:

Over the last ten seasons, the average annual ranking is 6.3 with an average of 48.4 AGLs per season. So, given that track record and the results last season, I could make an argument for fewer AGLs for the Vikings this season, but with a 9th overall ranking I'll stick with that being close enough to average that no adjustment to the win total this season is warranted.

As I've mentioned previously, I've had to slightly modify the sources for luck factors this year as one of the sources from last year stopped publishing their data. To determine luck factors, I am going again with the Luck Ratings from Team Rankings and using the differential between actual and estimated wins from the DVOA stats at FTN . I average the two numbers to get a game adjustment amount.

An example of a team winning a game they weren't expected to win based on luck factors and post-game win expectancy or estimated wins is the Vikings victory over the Bills a few years ago with Jefferson's iconic catch on 4th and 18 and Josh Allen fumbling the snap on the goal line. Neither is something likely to happen more often than not so while it was a game the Vikings won, it was also a game they would not be expected to win given the events of the game and the likelihood of them reoccurring that way (i.e. how many times out of 100 would Josh Allen fumble the snap at their one-yard line late in the game and the Vikings recover?).

The Vikings finished last season with a luck rating of +0.1 according to Team Rankings and estimated wins of 8.4 compared to actual 9 wins. Averaging those two results in +0.35 which is close enough to zero to not warrant an adjustment to this season's win total based on a reversion to the mean in luck factors.

The Vikings were tied for the 20th easiest schedule last season based on actual win-loss records of their opponents. This season, based on oddsmaker's over/under win totals for their opponents, the Vikings have the 16th easiest schedule. That's not much of a difference and therefore does not warrant any adjustment to their forecasted win total this season.

The Vikings start with two division games and a tougher matchup at Tampa Bay, followed by two easier matchups at the Saints and home against the Dolphins. The five-game stretch after their bye week is brutal- Colts, at Lions, Bills, at Packers, 49ers in Mexico City. That's the toughest five-game stretch I can remember in recent years. Fortunately, their schedule eases up after that, with just two road games among the final seven and perhaps only three tougher matchups against the Patriots, Lions, and Bears to end the regular season.

Overall, there was just one significant adjustment to the Vikings forecasted win total this season and that was three games due to the upgrade at quarterback from league bottom to just above average. Injuries, luck factors, and strength of schedule really weren't even close in terms of warranting adjustments.

But a significant upgrade at the most important position in sports warrants a three-game adjustment, leading to a season regular season record prediction for the Vikings of 12-5. That is 3.5 games above the Vikings over/under win total of 8.5 games and tied with my prediction for the Detroit Lions, so the division winner in this scenario would come down to tie-breakers.

As I look at the pundit landscape for the Vikings just ahead of the start of the regular season, there appears to be nearly universal expectations that Kyler Murray will be an upgrade at quarterback for the Vikings. The question is how much of an upgrade will he be. This Vikings team is the best team Murray has been a part of and so it's not outlandish for his performance to equal his better seasons in Arizona. And that would be a bit of an improvement over Sam Darnold in 2024 from a QBR standpoint.

There is also an upside scenario where based on a top five defense (which Murray has never had) a solid offensive line, a top-tier receiver group, and improved run game, Murray has a career year that puts him well into the top ten quarterback rankings. In that context it's important to note that the Vikings face the easiest schedule in terms of pass defenses this season according to Warren Sharp. (see graphic below).

There is also a downside scenario where things never quite click and/or he misses a lot of time due to injury.

There are former teammates and beat writers in Arizona that expect him to bounce back strong in Minnesota, but there are some others who question whether he is the right fit for Kevin O'Connell and the Vikings scheme and/or whether he has the drive to succeed in a new system at this point in his career. The latter is in the minority.

There are also many who expect the Vikings defense to regress this season. I don't see it. They point to the loss of Jonathan Greenard and Jonathan Allen and Javon Hargrave up front, and Harrison Smith (before his return was announced) in the back end. From what we've seen the last part of last season and so far in training camp and joint practices, there is no reason to believe that Dallas Turner is a downgrade from Greenard last season. And there is a chance he's an upgrade. Part of the reason the Vikings were willing to trade Greenard in the first place, besides financial considerations, was they felt Turner was ready to step up. And adding Kyle Van Noy provides experienced and proven depth.

I do think the losses of Hargrave and Allen will have a negative effect, especially earlier in the season as Domonique Orange and Caleb Banks ramp up, but I expect the dropoff will be small. Jalen Redmond is solid, Levi Drake-Rodriquez looks a bit stronger this year, and the combination of Tyrion-Ingram Dawkins and Elijah Williams should hold up reasonably well as Orange and Banks work more into the rotation.

At linebacker and the defensive secondary, the starting lineup is the same but depth is improved. Between James Pierre and Charles Demmings, we could see more three cornerbacks on the field with Byron Murphy Jr. in the slot more often, but with Harrison Smith, Josh Metellus, Theo Jackson, Jay Ward, Jacob Thomas, and Jakobe Thomas, there are plenty of safeties that can play and I wouldn't be surprised if we see more merit-based rotation there.

But some will argue that Brian Flores' blitz-happy scheme is bound to backfire on him eventually, but I really don't see that either. Flores' blitz scheme is much more nuanced and difficult to play against to the point where there are no simple counters.

On that topic, it's important to note that the Vikings defense faced the second-toughest schedule of opposing offenses last season by DVOA but despite that finished third in that metric. The Vikings defense also allowed the league's lowest explosive play rate (3.7%) despite facing opposing offenses that produced the highest explosive pass play rate and the fourth-highest explosive run play rate. They look to have a tough slate again this year- all the offenses in the division are good- but likely about the same as last season according to Warren Sharp's analysis:

It's also important to point out that the Vikings defense ranked third in DVOA last season (and 7th in points allowed) despite the Vikings offense producing the most turnovers in the league, having the lowest 3rd down conversion percentage in the league, and ranking 30th in time of possession. A more efficient offense would make the defense's job that much easier.

And beyond all that, Brian Flores has established a solid track record of top defenses since he became de facto defensive coordinator in New England, including all three seasons he's been in Minnesota.

From an analytics perspective, defensive results vary more year-to-year than offensive stats, but I'd argue that given the change in starting quarterback and Brian Flores as defensive coordinator with not that much roster turnover, there will be more variance in offensive results compared to last season than defensive results.

articles.title: Wales lock Carter cleared for Dragons after injury
articles.summary: Dragons co-captain Ben Carter fit for start of United Rugby Championship season after recovering from summer ankle injury suffered with Wales.
articles.body:
Dragons co-captain Ben Carter will be fit for the start of the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship (URC) after recovering from a summer ankle injury suffered with Wales.

The lock was ruled out of the Nations Championship defeat by South Africa in mid-July after a blow in training.

Carter, who had started Wales' six previous games, was on crutches and saw specialists on his return to Dragons.

The 25-year-old did not need surgery and is working towards his side's URC opener at Benetton on Friday, 25 September (19:45 BST).

"It's not an issue now. He is going really well and is probably in the best nick that I have seen him," said defence coach Dale MacLeod.

Carter made 17 appearances for Dragons last season – all of them starts – alongside nine games for his country in a breakthrough year in Test rugby.

"He is keen, refreshed and ready to get back into it but we are just doing the right thing and trying to get a good training load in him," added MacLeod.

"He will get enough smashing and bashing this season without jumping into it now. He is fit and ready to go for collisions and game time, but we are just keeping him out of it.

"If you look at his body shape, he is working really hard and has massive incentives heading into the World Cup next year."

Filo Tiatia's side ran in 13 tries in a pre-season friendly win against Hartpury on Saturday and step things up against Scarlets at Llandovery's Church Bank on Friday (19:00 BST).

Scrum-half Che Hope, who would have been a contender for Wales' summer tour were it not for a hamstring injury suffered in March, is poised to feature.

He was given the Hartpury game off while Morgan Lloyd, Rhodri Williams and summer signing Ere Enari shared duties, and all scored tries.

Tight-head prop Rob Hunt's strong first campaign with Dragons was ended by a ruptured hamstring at Ospreys at the end of January.

The South African had an operation and is also back in full training, but his workload will be managed.

Summer signing Terrell Peita, who will help fill the back-row void left by Wales number eight Aaron Wainwright , is currently playing for Northland in New Zealand's National Provincial Championship.

The regular season ends on 4 October with eight teams progressing to play-offs, which finish on 24 October.

Peita, who made his Super Rugby debut for Blues in May, will link up with Dragons after the tournament with a debut likely in December after the break for the Nations Championship.

"Northland are going very well and he is living the dream - not many boys get to win the Ranfurly Shield," said MacLeod, referring to the trophy that is currently held and defended by Peita's team.

"Terrell is playing well, which is really good, and contracts have a say in when players can come when seasons don't align, so that's just the way it works out."
