articles.title: O'Hare 'can't wait' for home Wrexham debut
articles.summary: Callum O'Hare "can't wait" to make his home debut after a hectic welcome to Wrexham since completing his deadline-day move from Sheffield United.  The 28-yea...
articles.body:
Callum O'Hare "can't wait" to make his home debut after a hectic welcome to Wrexham since completing his deadline-day move from Sheffield United.

The 28-year-old got up in the early hours on Tuesday morning to seal his switch to the Racecourse Ground before Wrexham's trip to Millwall.

O'Hare then raced to London on the train, arriving hours before kick-off to make the squad, but remained an unused sub as Wrexham won 3-0 at the Den.

Then came his first Welsh derby. He was thrust in from the start by Phil Parkinson, even though he had not yet trained with all of his new teammates.

And O'Hare very nearly capped off a whirlwind few days with his maiden Wrexham goal on debut at Swansea, but the former Coventry man dragged his chance wide.

"I probably should have had a goal, but I'm always going to be there, so hopefully that will come," former England youth international O'Hare admitted.

"I feel like I've settled in well. I'm yet to train with everyone, so hopefully, by doing so, I'll improve and get to know everyone's game."

He added: "It's been crazy, honestly. I woke up really early on deadline day to try to get everything done so I could be in the squad for the Wednesday game.

"Then I had to get the train up [to London]. The boys were already there. I got there for 5pm and still managed to be in the squad."

On the game at Swansea, O'Hare said: "I'm gutted that we didn't get three points, but they are a good team who keep the ball well.

"We just had to dig in, really, and concentrate for the whole game, which I think we did."

After having failed to keep a clean sheet in their first four games across all competitions, Wrexham have now kept back-to-back shutouts.

Four points earned from that win at Millwall and Saturday's draw with Swansea have the Red Dragons sat 11th in the Championship table.

And there will be no let-up for Wrexham as they face relegated sides Burnley and West Ham before the end of this week.

Parkinson's charges first host winless Burnley on Tuesday evening (19:45 BST) before another trip to the capital on Friday.

O'Hare, who previously scored at the Racecourse Ground as a Sheffield United player, is excited to play in front of the Wrexham faithful.

"It's perfect. That's what we play football for, we can't wait," he said.

"We want to go into Tuesday night full of confidence after two good away performances. Now we want to bring that to the Racecourse."

"When we played against Wrexham, especially at the Racecourse, that game was mental. As a player, you could feel the excitement and the passion from the pitch.

"It's something I'm looking forward to. I can't wait to go there, meet everyone and hopefully get the three points."

articles.title: Houston Dash can't overcome early deficit in road loss to Orlando Pride
articles.summary: Houston fell behind 14 minutes into the game and saw its deficit balloon in a loss to Orlando.
articles.body:
ORLANDO, Fla. - The Houston Dash fell behind early and couldn't catch up in a 3-1 loss to the Orlando Pride on Sunday night at Inter.co Stadium.

Houston (7-5-11, 26 points) fell behind just 14 minutes into the game and the deficit only grew. The Pride (9-2-12, 29) doubled its lead by halftime and pushed it to 3-0 near the midpoint of the second half.

The Dash's only goal came from Kiki Van Zanten in the 72nd minute, her fifth of the season, off an assist from Khyah Harper.

Orlando's goal scorers were Leah Klenke, Barbara Banda and Haley McCutcheon .

The match was delayed 90-plus minutes because of inclement weather in the Orlando area.

The Dash return home Saturday to host Utah Royals FC for a 7:45 p.m. kickoff at Shell Energy Stadium.

articles.title: Swansea must protect defensive record - Matos
articles.summary: Having conceded just once this season, head coach Vitor Matos says Swansea City must maintain their steely defensive record to challenge for promotion.
articles.body:
Swansea City head coach Vitor Matos has said his side must "take care" of their impressive defensive record as they aim to challenge for promotion.

Championship leaders Swansea have conceded just once across their first five games of the season, fewer than any other team in the English Football League (EFL).

A 0-0 draw against Wrexham means the Swans have managed four clean sheets in their first five league games for the first time since the 1978-79 season.

"It's good, but we know it can change quite quickly. We all know how the league is and how the results are," Matos said after Saturday's Welsh derby.

"That [defensive record] is something that we need to take care of, of course. It's important for us."

Speaking after a much-hyped but in the end somewhat lack-lustre affair at the Swansea.com Stadium, Matos says there is more to come from his side.

"We have said from the beginning that it is important to defend well to then be able to attack. That is the feeling that we want to have.

"Today was a massive game in terms of set-pieces. We knew they would be massive for Wrexham, and we didn't allow them that comfort in the game."

After Callum O'Hare had missed earlier on, Kieffer Moore nearly ended Swansea's clean-sheet run, but Lawrence Vigouroux denied the Wrexham forward.

Chile international Vigouroux has been gaining attention on social media for his distribution, but Matos also had praise for the keeper's shot-stopping ability.

"Clean sheets are massive. We all know that every player contributes to that, but Vigs is massive because he's a wonderful goalkeeper," Matos added.

"In a game when he didn't have a lot to do in the first-half, he made an unbelievable save in the second half. He is a goalie to do that."

Saturday's draw against Wrexham also saw the return of club captain Ben Cabango, whose tackle on debutant O'Hare caught the ire of Phil Parkinson.

Matos is pleased to have the Welsh international back from injury, and believes Cabango will add to the healthy competition for places in his backline.

Cabango featured in all but one of Swansea's Championship games last season while centre-back partner Cam Burgess played every minute of the campaign.

The Australia international is expected to miss the rest of this season with an Achilles injury, but Matos is confident he can keep his other options fresh.

"We have healthy competition, and it's important to have depth in that position," the Portuguese coach explained.

"Last season we coped for the whole season with Ben and Cam. It was quite a hard task for them. Having the depth there, which allows them to be fresh, is massive.

"Now we have Welshy (Stephen Welsh), Ben, Jenson [Seelt] and Fil [Lissah], which is nice to have and important for the upcoming games."

Swansea return to Championship action when they face Southampton at St Mary's on Tuesday, 8 September (19:45 BST).
